stem: Which protocol uses port 22?
explanation: SSH (Secure Shell) uses port 22. It gives an encrypted remote command-line connection and replaces insecure Telnet.
whyWrong: FTP uses ports 20 and 21 for file transfers.
Telnet uses port 23 and sends its session in plain text.
HTTPS uses port 443 for secure web traffic.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 4: TCP and UDP Ports and Protocols, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: Which of these would be used for streaming media?
explanation: User Datagram Protocol (UDP) is used for streaming media. It is connectionless, so it sends data without the handshakes and acknowledgments that slow TCP down.
whyWrong: TCP is connection oriented, and its acknowledgments and retransmissions make it a poor choice for streaming media.
RDP (Remote Desktop Protocol) is used to connect to and control other computers.
DHCP assigns IP addresses to clients automatically; it uses UDP but is not a transport for streaming.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 4: TCP and UDP Ports and Protocols, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: Which ports are used by the IMAP protocol?
explanation: Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP) uses port 143 by default and port 993 for its secure version. IMAP keeps mail on the server so it can sync across several devices.
whyWrong: Port 53 is DNS and port 68 is the DHCP client port.
Ports 80 and 443 are HTTP and HTTPS.
Ports 110 and 995 are POP3 and secure POP3.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 4: TCP and UDP Ports and Protocols, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: A user can receive email but cannot send any. Which protocol is not configured properly?
explanation: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) is probably not configured properly, because SMTP deals with sending mail. Receiving works, so the receiving protocol (POP3 or IMAP) is set up correctly.
whyWrong: POP3 receives mail, and receiving already works.
FTP transfers files to remote computers and has no part in sending email.
SNMP is used to manage and monitor network devices, not to send mail.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 4: TCP and UDP Ports and Protocols, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: Which of the following is the default inbound port of a DHCPv4 server?
explanation: The default inbound port of a DHCPv4 server is 67. Clients use port 68 for their side of the exchange.
whyWrong: Port 22 is the inbound port of an SSH server.
Port 995 is the secure inbound port of a POP3 server.
Port 3389 is the default inbound port of a server that runs RDP.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 4: TCP and UDP Ports and Protocols, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: Which of the following does HTTPS use to make a secure Internet connection?
explanation: HTTPS uses port 443 and makes its secure connection with Transport Layer Security (TLS) and an encrypted certificate. It is used by the majority of websites today.
whyWrong: Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) uses port 80 and sends data in plain text, so it is not secure.
SNMP is the standard for managing and monitoring devices on a network, not for securing web sessions.
SNMPv3 is the secure version of SNMP for device management, not the protocol that secures HTTPS.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 4: TCP and UDP Ports and Protocols, Cram Quiz question 6

stem: Which of the following is an advantage of UDP over TCP?
explanation: The main advantage of UDP over TCP is that it can transfer data packets faster. Because it is connectionless, it does not need the overhead of synchronization or sequencing that TCP uses. This makes it a faster option for streaming services, VoIP, and similar traffic.
whyWrong: Flow control is a TCP feature; UDP has none.
Connection handshakes (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK) are used by TCP, not UDP.
UDP is connectionless; TCP is the connection-based protocol.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 26

stem: Which protocol does Active Directory rely on most? (Select the best answer.)
explanation: Of the listed answers, Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) is relied upon most by Active Directory. LDAP deals with directory lists, such as the users in an Active Directory domain or the email addresses in an Exchange server. It uses port 389.
whyWrong: SMB (also called CIFS) provides shared access to files on any Windows computer, not just domain systems.
HTTPS transfers data securely from a web server to a browser.
DHCP provides IP address information to clients automatically.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 38

stem: Which of the following protocols is used to perform file sharing between Apple computers running macOS and PCs running Windows on a LAN?
explanation: SMB (Server Message Block) can be used for file sharing between Windows computers and computers running macOS. It is sometimes called by its older name, CIFS (Common Internet File System), and it uses port 445.
whyWrong: RDP (port 3389) is used to view or control remote computers.
SSH (port 22) makes secure connections to other systems and replaces Telnet.
POP3 (port 110) is used for downloading email.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 73

stem: You are planning a secure screened subnet (DMZ) that will incorporate several servers, including a web server, an FTP server, and a mail server. Which inbound ports will need to be opened at the firewall so that the servers can securely communicate with users on the Internet? (Select the four best answers.)
explanation: To meet the requirements securely, you could use SFTP on port 22, HTTPS on port 443, SMTP on port 587 for outbound mail, and POP3 on port 995 for inbound mail. SFTP rides on Secure Shell (SSH), and the other secure services use SSL/TLS. Standard FTP on port 21 is not secure; secure FTP uses SFTP (port 22) or FTPS (ports 989/990).
whyWrong: Port 21 is used by standard FTP, which is not secure.
Port 80 is HTTP, which sends web traffic without encryption.
Port 110 is POP3 without security.
Port 143 is IMAP without security.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 79
note: The book has 11 options (A–K). Three wrong ones (23, 53, 3389) are left out so the question fits the app's limit of 8 options.

stem: Which of the following protocols was designed to access information stored in an information directory, such as employee phonebooks?
explanation: Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) is designed to access information stored in a directory, typically known as an LDAP directory or LDAP database. This usually includes employee data and network configuration data, and LDAP uses port 389.
whyWrong: FTP is designed to transfer files between hosts.
RDP lets a user control a remote computer's desktop.
CIFS is used to share files and printers on a network.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 7: Introduction to TCP/IP, Review Questions question 2

stem: Which TCP/IP protocol uses port 80?
explanation: HTTP uses port 80. It carries unencrypted web traffic between browsers and web servers.
whyWrong: HTTPS uses port 443, not port 80.
Telnet uses port 23.
POP3 uses port 110.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 7: Introduction to TCP/IP, Review Questions question 3

stem: Which of the following protocols is responsible for sending email?
explanation: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) is responsible for sending email and uses port 25. Clients retrieve their mail with other protocols such as POP3 and IMAP.
whyWrong: IMAP4 is used to retrieve email from a server, not to send it.
POP3 downloads email from a server, not sends it.
SNMP is a network management protocol and is not related to email.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 7: Introduction to TCP/IP, Review Questions question 8

stem: What port does the RDP protocol work on?
explanation: Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) works on port 3389. RDP lets a user connect to and control a remote Windows computer.
whyWrong: Port 53 is used by DNS.
Port 143 is used by IMAP.
Port 389 is used by LDAP.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 7: Introduction to TCP/IP, Review Questions question 9

stem: What are advantages that TCP has over UDP? (Choose two.)
explanation: TCP is a connection-oriented protocol that establishes virtual circuits and acknowledges the delivery of packets. Because of these features, it has higher overhead than UDP and is a little slower.
whyWrong: UDP, not TCP, has faster delivery because it skips connection setup and acknowledgments.
UDP, not TCP, has lower overhead because it is connectionless.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 7: Introduction to TCP/IP, Review Questions question 11

stem: Your friend is concerned about the security of making an online purchase. What should you tell her to look for in the address bar of the web browser?
explanation: HTTP is inherently unsecure, but HTTPS encrypts the session with TLS and uses port 443. A URL that starts with https:// shows that the purchase data is encrypted in transit.
whyWrong: HTTP sends web traffic unencrypted, so it is the wrong thing to look for.
SSH is a secure protocol for remote command-line access, not for connecting to websites.
TLS is the encryption under HTTPS, but it is not what the browser shows in the address bar.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 7: Introduction to TCP/IP, Review Questions question 12

stem: Which of the following protocols is used for secure retrieval of email?
explanation: IMAP4 and POP3 are the two protocols used for email retrieval, and of the two only IMAP4 provides security features. IMAP also keeps messages on the server so they can be synchronized across devices.
whyWrong: SMTP sends email; it does not retrieve it.
LDAP is a directory services protocol, not an email protocol.
POP3 retrieves email but lacks the security features of IMAP4.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 7: Introduction to TCP/IP, Review Questions question 15

stem: Which network protocol is used for file and printer sharing and which port does it use?
explanation: Common Internet File System (CIFS) uses port 445 and is used to share files and printers on a network. Remote Desktop Protocol uses port 3389 and is used for remote computer administration.
whyWrong: RDP on port 3389 is for remote desktop control, not for file and printer sharing.
CIFS shares files and printers, but it uses port 445, not 3389.
Port 445 belongs to CIFS/SMB, and RDP is not a file-sharing protocol.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 7: Introduction to TCP/IP, Review Questions question 17

stem: Which of the following protocols can help an application store and manage user information on the network?
explanation: Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP, port 389) is the "phonebook" protocol of TCP/IP and helps applications store and manage user information. Directory services such as Active Directory use it.
whyWrong: SMTP (port 25) is an email-sending protocol.
NetBT (ports 137-139) lets computers communicate over the network using NetBIOS APIs.
SMB (port 445) is a file- and printer-sharing protocol.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 7: Introduction to TCP/IP, Review Questions question 19

stem: Your company hosts its own web server, and it allows consumers to make purchases via the server. The help line has been getting complaints that users are unable to access the website. You open the site from an internal workstation and it seems fine. What is the MOST LIKELY cause?
options: The firewall is blocking TCP port 23.
The firewall is blocking TCP port 443.
The security module of the web server is malfunctioning.
explanation: For secure transactions, the web server uses HTTPS, which uses TCP port 443. If the website works from an internal workstation, the server itself is fine, so the firewall is most likely blocking inbound traffic on port 443.
whyWrong: Port 23 is Telnet, which a web store does not use.
A faulty security module would also break the site for internal users, but the site works internally.
The site opens from an internal workstation, so the web server is not down.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 8: Network Services, Review Questions question 1

stem: You are configuring two email servers on your company's network. Which network protocol do the servers use to transfer mail to each other?
explanation: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) is used to transfer (send) email between servers. Mail servers use SMTP on port 25 to pass messages to each other.
whyWrong: POP3 is used by clients to download email, not by servers to transfer it.
IMAP4 is used by clients to retrieve email, not to move mail between servers.
SNMP is Simple Network Management Protocol and is not related to email.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 8: Network Services, Review Questions question 8

stem: What port does POP3 use?
explanation: Post Office Protocol 3 (POP3) uses port 110. POP3 downloads e-mail from a mail server to the client.
whyWrong: Port 22 is used by SSH and SFTP.
Port 42 is not used by POP3.
Port 256 is not assigned to POP3.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 21: The Internet, Chapter Review question 2

stem: Which protocol can you use to send e-mail?
explanation: You can use Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) to send e-mail messages. SMTP uses port 25.
whyWrong: IMAP is used to receive and manage e-mail on a server, not to send it.
POP3 is used to download e-mail from a server, not to send it.
PPP is a point-to-point link protocol, not an e-mail protocol.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 21: The Internet, Chapter Review question 4

stem: Which protocols can you use to receive e-mail? (Select two.)
explanation: You can use either Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP) or Post Office Protocol 3 (POP3) to receive e-mail messages. IMAP uses port 143 and POP3 uses port 110.
whyWrong: PPP is a point-to-point link protocol, not an e-mail protocol.
SMTP is used to send e-mail, not to receive it.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 21: The Internet, Chapter Review question 5

stem: Which of the following represent invalid port to protocol matchups? (Select two.)
explanation: Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) uses port 3389, not 3398. Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure (HTTPS) uses port 443; HTTP uses port 80.
whyWrong: SMB runs over port 445, and older NetBIOS-based SMB uses ports 137–139, so this matchup is valid.
SSH uses port 22, so this matchup is valid.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 21: The Internet, Chapter Review question 7
note: All-in-One 11e (220-1101/1102) Ch. 21: the current objectives list 137–139 as NetBIOS/NetBT and 445 as SMB/CIFS; the SMB matchup is still treated as valid.

stem: A systems administrator needs to use a protocol for secure remote access to network devices. Which of the following should they use?
explanation: Secure Shell (SSH) uses TCP port 22 and encrypts remote command-line sessions to network devices. It replaces the unsecure Telnet protocol.
whyWrong: Telnet sends the whole session, including passwords, in cleartext, so it is not secure.
RDP gives a graphical remote desktop session to Windows computers rather than command-line access to network devices.
SNMP on UDP port 161 monitors and manages devices; it is not a remote access protocol.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.1 question 1

stem: When an online store alerts you that you are being redirected to a secure server, what protocol should be seen in the URL?
explanation: Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure (HTTPS) is used to set up an encrypted session with a web server, so the URL starts with https://. It uses TCP port 443.
whyWrong: TFTP is a simple, unsecure file transfer protocol used to send configuration files and boot images.
HTTP sends web traffic unencrypted and is what the site uses before the redirect to the secure server.
SSH is used for secure remote command-line access, not for web pages in a browser.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.1 question 2

stem: Which of the following mail clients downloads the email, stores it on the local computer, and does not retain a copy on the mail server?
explanation: Post Office Protocol (POP3) downloads email to the local computer and by default deletes it from the server. It uses TCP port 110.
whyWrong: IMAP keeps the messages and folders on the mail server and synchronizes them across devices.
SMTP sends and relays mail between servers; it does not download mail to a client.
SSH is a secure remote access protocol, not an email protocol.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.1 question 3

stem: Which port is used by the application protocol that Windows operating systems use for file and print sharing?
explanation: Server Message Block (SMB) provides file and printer sharing in Windows and uses TCP port 445. Older Windows networks also used NetBIOS over TCP/IP on ports 137-139.
whyWrong: Ports 137-139 are used by NetBIOS over TCP/IP for legacy name and session services, not by modern SMB.
Ports 67 and 68 are used by DHCP to assign IP addresses to clients.
Port 389 is used by LDAP to query and update directory services.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.1 question 4

stem: Which of the following standard ports is used by secure Post Office Protocol (POP)?
explanation: Port 995 is the standard port for POP3 over SSL/TLS (POP3S). Unsecure POP3 uses port 110.
whyWrong: Port 110 is used by unsecure POP3.
Port 993 is used by secure IMAP (IMAPS), not secure POP.
Port 143 is used by unsecure IMAP.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.1 question 5

stem: Which of the following protocols is connectionless and used for streaming video or audio?
explanation: User Datagram Protocol (UDP) is connectionless and sends data without a handshake or acknowledgments. This low overhead makes it suited to streaming video and audio, where speed matters more than resending lost packets.
whyWrong: TCP is connection-oriented, and its acknowledgments and retransmissions add delay that streaming does not need.
RDP is a remote desktop protocol for Windows computers, not a transport protocol for streaming.
TFTP is a simple file transfer protocol that runs over UDP; it is not used for streaming media.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.1 question 6

stem: Which of the following protocols uses TCP ports 20/21 and transfers data in cleartext?
explanation: File Transfer Protocol (FTP) uses TCP port 21 for control and port 20 for data, and it sends data and credentials in cleartext. Secure alternatives are SFTP (over SSH, port 22) and FTPS (FTP over TLS).
whyWrong: TFTP uses UDP port 69, not TCP ports 20 and 21.
SSH uses TCP port 22 and encrypts its traffic.
FTPS is FTP secured with TLS, so it does not send data in cleartext.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.1 question 8

stem: Which of the following are default ports for HTTP and HTTPS traffic? (Choose two.)
explanation: Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) uses TCP port 80, and HTTPS uses TCP port 443. Web servers listen on these ports by default.
whyWrong: Port 23 is used by Telnet.
Port 110 is used by POP3.
Port 445 is used by SMB file sharing.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.1 question 9

stem: TCP is connection-orientated and uses a three-way handshake. What is the correct sequence of the handshake?
explanation: The TCP three-way handshake is SYN, then SYN-ACK, then ACK. The client sends a SYN, the server answers with a SYN-ACK, and the client confirms with an ACK before data flows.
whyWrong: The SYN-ACK is the server's reply to a SYN, so it cannot come last.
SIGNAL, CONNECT, and ACKNOWLEDGE are not TCP flags.
A SYN-ACK can only answer a SYN, so the handshake cannot start with it.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.1 question 10

stem: A system administrator is setting up a new firewall and needs to allow SMTP traffic to flow through. Which of the following TCP ports must be enabled for inbound traffic?
explanation: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) uses TCP port 25 to send and relay email between mail servers. The firewall must allow inbound port 25 for the mail server to receive mail.
whyWrong: Port 21 is the FTP control port.
Port 22 is used by SSH, SFTP, and SCP.
Port 23 is used by Telnet.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.1 question 11

stem: Which of the following standard ports is used by secure IMAP?
explanation: Port 993 is the standard port for IMAP over SSL/TLS (IMAPS). Unsecure IMAP uses port 143.
whyWrong: Port 110 is used by unsecure POP3.
Port 995 is used by secure POP3, not secure IMAP.
Port 143 is used by unsecure IMAP.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.1 question 12

stem: Which of the following is an unsecure remote access protocol that can have its password stolen by a protocol analyzer?
explanation: Telnet (TCP port 23) sends the whole session, including the user name and password, in cleartext. A protocol analyzer that captures the traffic can read the password, so SSH should be used instead.
whyWrong: SSL is an encryption protocol for securing connections, not a remote access protocol.
SSH encrypts the session, so a protocol analyzer cannot read the password.
RDP encrypts its remote desktop sessions by default.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.1 question 13

stem: Which port is commonly used for transferring files between a client and a server?
explanation: FTP uses port 21 for transferring files between a client and a server. It lets users upload, download, and manage files on remote servers.
whyWrong: Port 143 is IMAP, which an email client uses to read mail on a server.
Port 80 is HTTP, which is used to retrieve web pages.
Port 25 is SMTP, which sends email between mail servers.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 22
note: Neil Core 1 mock exam (220-1101).

stem: Which network protocol is used for secure remote access and secure file transfers?
explanation: Secure Shell (SSH), on port 22, gives encrypted remote access to a server's command line. It also carries secure file transfers such as SFTP and SCP.
whyWrong: SNMP is used to monitor and manage network devices.
POP is used to download email from a mail server.
NTP synchronizes the time on network devices.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 23
note: Neil Core 1 mock exam (220-1101).

stem: Which network protocol is commonly used for insecure remote command-line access to a server?
explanation: Telnet, on port 23, gives remote command-line access to a server, but it sends everything, including passwords, as plain text. SSH has replaced it for secure remote access.
whyWrong: DNS translates domain names into IP addresses.
HTTP is used to retrieve web pages.
SNMP is used to monitor and manage network devices.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 24
note: Neil Core 1 mock exam (220-1101).

stem: Which network protocol is primarily used for sending email messages between mail servers?
explanation: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) is the standard protocol for sending email between mail servers, on port 25. It carries mail from the sender's server to the recipient's server, and clients then read it with POP3 or IMAP.
whyWrong: FTP is used for file transfers.
HTTP is used to retrieve web pages.
POP downloads email from a server to a client; it does not send mail.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 25
note: Neil Core 1 mock exam (220-1101). Stem reworded: the book asked for 'sending and receiving', but SMTP only sends; POP3/IMAP receive.

stem: Which network protocol is responsible for translating domain names into IP addresses?
explanation: The Domain Name System (DNS) translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses. This lets users reach websites and services by name instead of remembering IP addresses.
whyWrong: DHCP assigns IP addresses to devices on a network.
HTTP is used to retrieve web pages.
SNMP is used to monitor and manage network devices.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 26
note: Neil Core 1 mock exam (220-1101).

stem: Which network protocol is responsible for automatically assigning IP addresses to devices on a network?
explanation: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) automatically assigns IP addresses to devices on a network. It also gives them other settings, such as the subnet mask, default gateway, and DNS server addresses.
whyWrong: SNMP is used to monitor and manage network devices.
DNS translates domain names into IP addresses.
HTTP is used to retrieve web pages.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 27
note: Neil Core 1 mock exam (220-1101).

stem: Which of the following would a company MOST LIKELY use for authentication to a server room?
explanation: Radio-frequency identification (RFID) is commonly used for access to areas of a building such as a server room. It is often implemented as a proximity-based ID card or badge. The other options are not usually associated with authentication.
whyWrong: 802.11ac is a Wi-Fi standard that runs on 5 GHz, not an access-control method.
Fixed wireless is a service that provides Internet access to a building or home.
MIMO uses multiple antennas to increase data transfer in 802.11n and 802.11ac networks.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 5: Wireless Technologies, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: Which standard can attain a data transfer rate of 1 Gbps over a wireless connection?
explanation: 802.11ac (and 802.11ax) can attain speeds in excess of 1 Gbps over wireless. Older Wi-Fi standards top out at 54 Mbps or less.
whyWrong: 802.11a has a typical maximum of 54 Mbps.
802.11b, rarely used today, has a maximum of 11 Mbps.
802.11g has a typical maximum of 54 Mbps.
802.3ab (1000BASE-T) is 1 Gbps over twisted pair cable, which is wired, not wireless.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 5: Wireless Technologies, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: Which of the following is often broken down into groups of channels including 1–5, 6–10, and 11?
explanation: In the United States, the 2.4 GHz frequency range is broken into three groups: channels 1–5, 6–10, and 11. By placing separate wireless networks on distant channels (such as 1 and 11), you can avoid overlapping and interference.
whyWrong: 802.11ac is a Wi-Fi standard, not a frequency band.
5 GHz uses channels such as 36, 40, 149, and 153.
802.11a is a Wi-Fi standard, not a frequency band.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 5: Wireless Technologies, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: You are servicing a customer with a cable broadband Internet connection and an 802.11ac wireless network that is experiencing interference from a nearby office. The customer’s WAP is mounted to the ceiling. Which of the following is the easiest and BEST solution?
options: Move the wireless access point to another location.
Reconfigure the WAP to use 2.4 GHz instead of 5 GHz.
Change the broadcasting channel on the WAP to one that is not used by any neighbors.
Recommend a long-range fixed wireless service.
explanation: The easiest and best solution is to change the WAP's broadcasting channel to one that no neighbor uses. That first requires a wireless site survey to find out which channels are in use. If you survey anyway, you can find an open channel on the 5 GHz band.
whyWrong: Moving the access point could work, but it takes hands-on work because the WAP is mounted to the ceiling.
Switching to 2.4 GHz does not ensure less interference, because channel overlap is more likely on 2.4 GHz than on 5 GHz.
Long-range fixed wireless is the most expensive and difficult option, and the customer already has broadband Internet access.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 5: Wireless Technologies, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: Which wireless system is composed of readers and tags and can be used for access control, commerce, advertising, manufacturing, and agriculture?
explanation: Radio-frequency identification (RFID) is a wireless technology that uses readers to get information stored on tags. It is used for access control, commerce, advertising, manufacturing, and agriculture.
whyWrong: 802.11ax is a Wi-Fi standard that uses the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands.
Wi-Fi 6 is the name for the 802.11ax wireless LAN standard, not a tag-and-reader system.
The FCC is the US agency that regulates wireless frequency use, not a wireless system.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 5: Wireless Technologies, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: Which of the following allows multiple devices to both transmit and receive data simultaneously dramatically increasing network capacity compared to previous standards? (Select all that apply.)
explanation: Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) allows multiple devices to both transmit and receive data simultaneously, which dramatically increases network capacity. It supports 16×16 MU-MIMO, double the spatial streams of Wi-Fi 6.
whyWrong: Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) supports only 8 spatial streams, half as many as Wi-Fi 7.
A WISP is an Internet service provider that uses wireless technology to connect subscribers, not a Wi-Fi standard.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 5: Wireless Technologies, Cram Quiz question 6

stem: Which Wi-Fi standard was the first to introduce support for the 6 GHz frequency band, significantly reducing interference from legacy devices?
explanation: Wi-Fi 6E is the first Wi-Fi standard to extend Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) into the 6 GHz frequency band. The new band adds spectrum and reduces congestion from older devices on the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands.
whyWrong: Wi-Fi 5 (802.11ac) operates only in the 5 GHz band.
Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) without the E is limited to the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands.
Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) also uses 6 GHz, but it came after Wi-Fi 6E.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 81

stem: Which of the following wireless communication standards is often described in terms of a wireless personal area network?
explanation: Bluetooth networks are often called wireless personal area networks (WPANs). Bluetooth connects devices that are close to one person, such as headsets, keyboards, and phones, over a short range.
whyWrong: Infrared is a line-of-sight technology that has largely disappeared and is not usually described as a WPAN standard.
Cellular technology connects devices to a carrier's wide area network, not a personal area network.
Ethernet is a wired LAN standard, not a wireless technology.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 6: Networking Fundamentals, Review Questions question 10

stem: Which of the following legacy wireless IEEE standards operate on the 2.4 GHz radio frequency and are directly compatible with each other? (Choose two.)
explanation: Both 802.11b and 802.11g operate in the 2.4 GHz range and use similar transmission standards, so they are compatible with each other. 802.11g raised the speed to 54 Mbps while staying backward compatible with 802.11b.
whyWrong: 802.11a operates in the 5 GHz range, not 2.4 GHz.
802.11ac operates in the 5 GHz range, not 2.4 GHz.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 9: Wireless and SOHO Networking, Review Questions question 1

stem: Which of the following are features that allow 802.11ac to achieve higher data throughput? (Choose two.)
explanation: 802.11ac achieves high throughput with channel bonding and MIMO. Channel bonding combines several smaller channels into one wider channel, and MIMO uses multiple antennas for multiple inputs and outputs.
whyWrong: 802.11ac uses beamforming, but it improves range and signal focus rather than throughput.
Code division multiplexing is a cellular technique, not an 802.11ac throughput feature.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 9: Wireless and SOHO Networking, Review Questions question 3

stem: You are upgrading a wireless network from Wi-Fi 5 over to Wi-Fi 6. Which of the following statements is not correct?
options: Fewer users will be able to use each access point.
Devices may have lower power usage while using the network.
explanation: Wi-Fi 6 is faster than Wi-Fi 5, and its range is similar. More users, not fewer, can use each access point, and devices may use less power thanks to a new sleep feature (target wake time).
whyWrong: This statement is correct, because Wi-Fi 6 gives faster speeds than Wi-Fi 5.
This statement is correct, because the range of Wi-Fi 6 is similar to Wi-Fi 5.
This statement is correct, because Wi-Fi 6 can lower device power use with its sleep feature.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 9: Wireless and SOHO Networking, Review Questions question 5

stem: You are configuring a single 802.11g wireless network that has been having intermittent communications issues. The office space is large enough that it has three WAPs. What channels should you configure the WAPs on to avoid communication issues?
explanation: The 2.4 GHz band has 14 channels, but in North America only channels 1 through 11 are allowed. The three nonoverlapping channels are 1, 6, and 11, so access points on those channels do not interfere with each other.
whyWrong: Channels 2, 5, and 7 overlap with each other, so the access points would interfere.
Channel 14 is not allowed in North America, and channel 8 overlaps neighboring channels.
Channels 3, 6, and 9 overlap with each other, so the access points would interfere.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 9: Wireless and SOHO Networking, Review Questions question 9

stem: You are setting up a wireless network. Which wireless standards would give the users over 1 Gbps throughput? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: 802.11be (Wi-Fi 7, up to 46 Gbps) and 802.11ac (up to 6.9 Gbps) both give users more than 1 Gbps. 802.11ax would do so as well, although it is not listed.
whyWrong: 802.11g tops out at 54 Mbps, far below 1 Gbps.
802.11n tops out at 600 Mbps, which is below 1 Gbps.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 9: Wireless and SOHO Networking, Review Questions question 10

stem: Which of the following technologies can operate in the 125 kHz to 134 kHz range?
explanation: Radio-frequency identification (RFID) can operate in three frequency bands: 125 kHz to 134 kHz, 13.56 MHz, or 856 MHz to 960 MHz. The low-frequency band is common for access badges and animal tags.
whyWrong: Bluetooth operates at 2.4 GHz.
NFC operates at 13.56 MHz.
LTE operates between 600 MHz and 6 GHz.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 9: Wireless and SOHO Networking, Review Questions question 12

stem: Due to channel interference, you are upgrading a wireless network from Wi-Fi 5 to Wi-Fi 6. Which feature of Wi-Fi 6 reduces channel interference?
explanation: The Wi-Fi 6 feature that reduces channel interference is Basic Service Set (BSS) coloring, which adds a field to the wireless frame that distinguishes it from frames of nearby networks. Devices can then ignore overlapping traffic from other networks on the same channel.
whyWrong: OFDMA improves speed by letting an access point transmit to multiple clients at once.
MU-MIMO increases speed, and in Wi-Fi 6 it works for uplink as well as downlink connections.
DFS was introduced earlier and detects radar interference to change frequencies, not to separate neighboring Wi-Fi networks.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 9: Wireless and SOHO Networking, Review Questions question 13

stem: Which was the first Wi-Fi version to support WPA3 and OFDMA?
explanation: Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) was the first standard to support WPA3 security and OFDMA modulation. Wi-Fi 6E is the same standard extended into the 6 GHz band.
whyWrong: Wi-Fi 5 (802.11ac) supports neither OFDMA nor required WPA3.
Wi-Fi 6E added the 6 GHz band to features that Wi-Fi 6 had already introduced.
Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) came later and builds on features that Wi-Fi 6 introduced.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 9: Wireless and SOHO Networking, Review Questions question 15

stem: Besides 802.11 standards, which wireless communication method also works in the 2.4 GHz range?
explanation: Bluetooth also operates in the 2.4 GHz range. Bluetooth devices hop between frequencies in that band to reduce interference with Wi-Fi.
whyWrong: Satellite links use much higher microwave frequencies, not the 2.4 GHz band.
5G cellular mmWave operates between 24 GHz and 86 GHz.
NFC operates at 13.56 MHz.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 9: Wireless and SOHO Networking, Review Questions question 19

stem: Which of the following 802.11 standards functions only on the 5-GHz band?
explanation: The 802.11ac standard works only on the 5-GHz band. 802.11g works on 2.4 GHz, 802.11n works on both bands, and 802.11i is the security standard behind WPA2.
whyWrong: 802.11g works only on the 2.4-GHz band.
802.11n works on both the 2.4-GHz and the 5-GHz bands.
802.11i is a security standard (WPA2), not a radio standard on any band.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 20: Wireless Networking, Chapter Review question 1

stem: What’s the top speed for data transfers using 802.11ac technology?
explanation: Data transfers using 802.11ac top out at around 1+ Gbps. It reaches these speeds on the 5-GHz band with wide channels and MU-MIMO.
whyWrong: 1+ Mbps is about the speed of the original 802.11 standard, far below 802.11ac.
11+ Mbps is about the speed of 802.11b.
11+ Gbps is far beyond what 802.11ac can deliver.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 20: Wireless Networking, Chapter Review question 7

stem: Bluetooth technology is most often used to link computers into what sort of network?
explanation: Bluetooth most often creates personal area networks (PANs). A PAN links devices close to one person, such as headsets, keyboards, and phones.
whyWrong: Bluetooth area network is not a real network type.
A LAN covers a building or office and is usually built with Ethernet or Wi-Fi, not Bluetooth.
A WAN spans long distances, far beyond Bluetooth's short range.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 20: Wireless Networking, Chapter Review question 8

stem: Which of the following standards work with radios that are single-band 2.4 GHz? (Select all that apply.)
explanation: 802.11b, 802.11g, Wi-Fi 4 (802.11n), and Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) can all use the 2.4 GHz band, so they work with single-band 2.4 GHz radios. Wi-Fi 5 (802.11ac) uses only the 5 GHz band.
whyWrong: Wi-Fi 5 (802.11ac) works only in the 5 GHz band.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.3 question 1

stem: Which of the following wireless standards supports both 5 GHz and 2.4 GHz?
explanation: Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) works in both the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands, which gives it more channels to use. Wi-Fi 6E adds the 6 GHz band as well.
whyWrong: 802.11b works only in the 2.4 GHz band.
802.11g works only in the 2.4 GHz band.
802.11a works only in the 5 GHz band.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.3 question 2

stem: A user is trying and failing to get their Bluetooth earbuds to connect to their smartphone to listen to music. Which of the following actions should the user carry out? (Choose two.)
options: Go to Settings | Wi-Fi, then enable Bluetooth
Go to Settings | Mobile Data, then enable Bluetooth
Go to Settings, then enable Bluetooth
explanation: The user must turn Bluetooth on in the phone's Settings and then pair the earbuds with the phone. Pairing links the two devices so they can connect.
whyWrong: Bluetooth is not turned on from the Wi-Fi settings page; it has its own setting.
Bluetooth is not turned on from the mobile data settings; mobile data controls the cellular internet connection.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.3 question 3
note: Book answer corrected: the question asks for two actions and the book's explanation names both (enable Bluetooth, then pair), but the key marked only enabling Bluetooth.

stem: Which of the following wireless protocols can be used for contactless payments?
explanation: Near-field communication (NFC) works over a few centimeters and is used for contactless payments with phones, watches, and cards. The short range makes it hard to intercept by accident.
whyWrong: Bluetooth connects devices such as headsets and speakers; it is not used for tap-to-pay payments.
RFID tags are used to track and identify items such as stock and badges, not for payments from a phone.
Tethering shares a phone's cellular internet connection with another device.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.3 question 5

stem: Which of the following standards supports only the 5GHz frequency band?
explanation: 802.11a works only in the 5 GHz band, at up to 54 Mbps. 802.11b and 802.11g use only 2.4 GHz, and 802.11n can use both bands.
whyWrong: 802.11b works only in the 2.4 GHz band.
802.11g works only in the 2.4 GHz band.
802.11n can use both 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.3 question 6

stem: Which of the following statements about the 2.4 GHz wireless frequency are true? (Choose two.)
explanation: The 2.4 GHz band has lower data rates than 5 GHz but covers a greater distance and passes through walls better. The 5 GHz band is faster and has more channels but a shorter range.
whyWrong: 5 GHz gives higher data rates than 2.4 GHz.
2.4 GHz has the longer range, because lower frequencies travel farther and pass through obstacles better.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.3 question 7

stem: Which of the following wireless technologies has the fastest throughput?
explanation: Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) has the highest throughput of these standards, with a theoretical maximum of about 9.6 Gbps. Wi-Fi 5 (802.11ac) reaches several gigabits per second in theory, 802.11a 54 Mbps, and 802.11b 11 Mbps.
whyWrong: 802.11ac (Wi-Fi 5) is fast but slower than its successor 802.11ax.
802.11a has a maximum of 54 Mbps.
802.11b has a maximum of only 11 Mbps.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.3 question 8
note: Book explanation corrected: it gave 3.5 Gbps for 802.11ax (the theoretical maximum is about 9.6 Gbps) and named 802.11c for 802.11ac.

stem: Which of the following wireless standards is backward-compatible with 802.11g?
explanation: 802.11n works in the 2.4 GHz band as well as 5 GHz, so an 802.11n access point also supports 802.11g (and 802.11b) clients. 802.11g is in turn backward-compatible with 802.11b.
whyWrong: 802.11b is the older standard that 802.11g supports; it cannot run 802.11g connections itself.
802.11a uses the 5 GHz band, so it cannot talk to 2.4 GHz 802.11g devices.
802.11ac uses only the 5 GHz band, so it cannot talk to 2.4 GHz 802.11g devices.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.3 question 9
note: Book answer "802.11b" corrected to 802.11n: a newer standard is backward-compatible with an older one in the same band (802.11n supports 802.11g clients); 802.11g is backward-compatible with 802.11b, not the reverse. Typo 801.11ac fixed.

stem: Which of the following statements about the 5 GHz wireless frequency are true? (Choose two.)
options: 5GHz is more effective at propagating through solid surfaces than 2.4GHz
5GHz is less effective at propagating through solid surfaces than 2.4GHz
5GHz supports more individual channels and suffers less congestion than 2.4GHz
5GHz supports more individual channels and suffers more congestion than 2.4GHz
explanation: 5 GHz signals pass through walls and other solid surfaces less well than 2.4 GHz signals. The 5 GHz band has many more non-overlapping channels, so it suffers less congestion than 2.4 GHz.
whyWrong: 2.4 GHz, not 5 GHz, passes through solid surfaces better.
With more channels to spread across, 5 GHz has less congestion, not more.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.3 question 10

stem: Which of the following standards supports MIMO technology?
explanation: 802.11n (Wi-Fi 4) introduced multiple input, multiple output (MIMO), which sends several data streams at once over multiple antennas. It works in both the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands.
whyWrong: 802.11a uses a single antenna stream in the 5 GHz band and has no MIMO.
802.11b is a 2.4 GHz standard from before MIMO.
802.11g is a 2.4 GHz standard from before MIMO.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.3 question 11
note: Book explanation corrected: it called 802.11n's dual-band operation MIMO; MIMO is the use of multiple antennas and streams.

stem: Which of the following BEST describes the use of the licensed band in wireless communication?
options: A reserved frequency spectrum for authorized users
An unlicensed frequency spectrum for general use
explanation: A licensed band is a frequency range that a regulator reserves for authorized users with specific licenses, which gives controlled operation with little interference. Wi-Fi uses unlicensed bands such as 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz instead.
whyWrong: A publicly accessible spectrum describes an unlicensed band, not a licensed one.
Licensed bands are long-term allocations to licensees, not temporary experimental use.
An unlicensed spectrum is the opposite of a licensed band.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.7 question 4
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.7 (network troubleshooting) = current 5.5. Tagged to current 2.2 channels (regulations), the closest topic.

stem: Which wireless network standard offers the highest data transfer rates?
explanation: Of the standards listed, 802.11ac (Wi-Fi 5) has the highest data rates. It runs in the 5 GHz band and supports multiple spatial streams with wide channels, so it is much faster than 802.11a, b, and g.
whyWrong: 802.11a supports at most 54 Mbps in the 5 GHz band.
802.11b supports at most 11 Mbps in the 2.4 GHz band.
802.11g supports at most 54 Mbps in the 2.4 GHz band.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 20
note: Neil Core 1 mock exam (220-1101).

stem: While looking at the details of a server in your provider’s control panel, you notice that it says “Apache” in the HTTP summary. What kind of server is this?
explanation: Apache is a type of web server that runs on Linux. It is also known as Apache HTTP Server.
whyWrong: File servers store and transfer files but do not serve websites.
Email servers send and receive mail with POP3, IMAP, and SMTP.
Authentication servers verify the identity of users and computers logging in to the network.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 6: Networked Hosts, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: Which type of server acts as a go-between for clients and websites?
explanation: A proxy server acts as a go-between for clients and websites. It is a caching server that stores commonly accessed websites, and it often runs as a standalone server.
whyWrong: A print server manages network printers and the spooling and priority of print jobs.
A syslog server gathers logging data from network devices for analysis.
A DHCP server hands out IP addresses and other TCP/IP settings to clients.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 6: Networked Hosts, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: Which type of server runs Microsoft Exchange?
explanation: Microsoft Exchange is a type of email server software. You could run several services on one server, but unless the office is small, each server role should be a separate system.
whyWrong: A file server stores and shares files, not mail.
An authentication server verifies the identity of users and computers.
A web server delivers websites to browsers, not mail.
SCADA is not a server; it is a system that controls infrastructure such as heating, cooling, and electricity.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 6: Networked Hosts, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: Which type of device category would a smart thermostat fall under?
explanation: A smart thermostat is a type of Internet of Things (IoT) device. IoT devices are everyday objects that connect to the network so they can be monitored and controlled.
whyWrong: SCADA is an industrial system that controls an organization's infrastructure facilities.
A load balancer distributes IP traffic among multiple servers.
A spam gateway filters unwanted junk email for the accounts on a network.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 6: Networked Hosts, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: You have been tasked with installing a solution that will cache and monitor Internet traffic. Which of the following devices is the BEST solution?
explanation: A proxy server is the best solution because it monitors, controls, and caches Internet traffic. It acts as an intermediary between the LAN and external networks and adds security for the LAN.
whyWrong: An AAA server verifies and manages user access; it does not cache web traffic.
An authentication server identifies users and grants or denies access.
A spam gateway filters and blocks unwanted email, not general Internet traffic.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 6: Networked Hosts, Cram Quiz question 5

stem:
You are working in a command line and see the following results:

```
example.com = 93.184.216.34
```
Which of the following server types has MOST LIKELY helped supply this information to you?
explanation: The Domain Name System (DNS) server resolves domain names such as example.com to their IP addresses. It maps user-friendly names to network resources. Commands such as ping, tracert, nslookup, and dig use it to show this information.
whyWrong: A DHCP server hands out IP addresses to clients automatically.
An authentication server, such as a domain controller running LDAP, verifies the identity of users who log in.
A syslog server gathers logs from network devices for an admin.
A print server manages one or more printers on the network.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 20

stem: What is the term for devices that have an integrated CPU and RAM and are part of the Internet of Things (IoT), such as smart security systems and fire alarms, medical sensors, and appliances?
explanation: Embedded systems are devices with an integrated CPU and RAM that process information internally without a controlling system. They are found in home appliances, office automation, thin clients, security systems, medical and automotive devices, and more. They make up a large part of the Internet of Things.
whyWrong: A syslog server collects logged event information sent by routers and other network devices.
A web server houses an organization's website.
An IDS detects unauthorized access attempts and an IPS also tries to stop them.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 58

stem: Which of the following are commonly found in electrical power grids, water treatment plants, gas/oil pipelines, hydroelectric systems, sewage systems, and traffic systems and must be heavily secured because they are often used in protected environments and infrastructures?
explanation: Supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems are found in power grids, water treatment plants, pipelines, sewage and traffic systems, building controls, and similar infrastructure. Compared to home and small office systems, SCADA solutions must be heavily secured because they run protected environments and infrastructures.
whyWrong: A router gives access from one network to another.
A load balancer routes client requests evenly across servers so none is overloaded or idle.
A spam gateway protects the network from spam email, usually just behind the firewall.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 70

stem: Which of the following LAN hosts would MOST LIKELY provide the services needed to allow multiple clients access to cached Internet web pages?
explanation: A proxy server provides the services needed for multiple clients to access cached Internet web pages. It is normally located on the LAN, so it is known as a LAN host or network host.
whyWrong: A file server stores files such as documents and spreadsheets for clients, not cached web pages.
A web server provides web pages but normally sits on the Internet, an intranet, or a screened subnet, not on the LAN as a host for clients.
A DNS server resolves domain names to IP addresses and does not cache web pages.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 76

stem: Why is Network Time Protocol (NTP) considered a critical service in network environments?
options: It ensures timestamp accuracy for security policies and log correlation across systems.
It automatically adjusts firewall rules based on time-sensitive threat levels.
It coordinates scheduled updates and software rollouts across multiple devices.
It helps enforce time-based access control for users on shared systems.
explanation: NTP ensures timestamp accuracy for security policies and log correlation across systems. Its main role is to synchronize the clocks of devices across a network. Accurate time is crucial for consistent logs, time-based authentication, and secure operations.
whyWrong: Some firewalls support time-based rules, but the firewall software, not NTP, controls them.
Updates and rollouts are scheduled by patch management or systems management tools, not by NTP.
Time-based access control is enforced by authentication or policy systems; NTP only provides the accurate time.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 82

stem: Your manager wants you to install a networked Internet appliance that prevents network traffic–based attacks and includes antimalware and antispam software. What should you install?
explanation: The manager wants a unified threat management (UTM) device. UTM devices are designed to be one-stop network protection, combining a firewall, intrusion prevention, antimalware, and antispam features.
whyWrong: A spam gateway helps with spam email but does not stop other attacks or malware.
A load balancer spreads work across multiple servers.
A proxy server makes requests on behalf of clients.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 8: Network Services, Review Questions question 2

stem: You are installing a file server for the accounting department. Where should this file server be located on the network?
explanation: If the data on the server does not need to be accessed from the Internet, the server should be in the most secure place possible, which is inside the firewall in the secure network. The screened subnet is also behind a firewall, but it is partly open to the outside world, so it is less secure than the internal network.
whyWrong: Outside the firewall the server would have no protection from the Internet.
The screened subnet is partly open to the outside world, so it is less secure than the internal network.
A router is a network device, not a place to host a file server.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 8: Network Services, Review Questions question 3

stem: Which of the following are services that a print server should provide? (Choose two.)
options: Providing clients with the appropriate printer driver during installation
Notifying users when the print job is complete
explanation: Print servers make printers available to clients, accept print jobs, process them, and manage print priorities. They also provide client computers with the right print drivers when the clients install the printer.
whyWrong: Print servers do not turn printers off on demand.
Print servers are not responsible for notifying users that a job has printed.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 8: Network Services, Review Questions question 4

stem: Which type of server is responsible for preventing users from accessing websites with objectionable content?
explanation: A proxy server can be configured to block access to websites that contain potentially dangerous or inflammatory material. Because it makes web requests on behalf of clients, it can filter what they reach.
whyWrong: Web servers host web pages, some of which may have objectionable content.
DHCP servers provide clients with IP addresses.
DNS servers resolve hostnames to IP addresses.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 8: Network Services, Review Questions question 5

stem: You have five web servers that manage requests for online purchases. An administrator notices that one of the severs is always busy while another is idle, and the company is getting some online complaints about the slow website. Which of the following servers will help fix this?
explanation: A load balancer spreads the work across multiple servers. It accepts each inbound request and sends it to the most appropriate web server, so no single server is overloaded while others sit idle.
whyWrong: DNS resolves hostnames to IP addresses.
DHCP provides IP configuration information.
A proxy makes requests, usually outbound, on behalf of clients.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 8: Network Services, Review Questions question 9

stem: A computer using which of the following would be considered a legacy device? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: Legacy systems use older hardware, software, or network protocols that are not commonly used today. A 386 processor, the IPX/SPX protocol, and an application from 1983 all fit that description.
whyWrong: A system with only 1 GB of RAM may be underpowered, but that alone does not make it a legacy system.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 8: Network Services, Review Questions question 10

stem: An administrator sets up an NTP server on their local network. What is the purpose of an NTP server on the local network?
options: To query national NTP servers to ensure all computers on the local network are set to the same time
To provide the correct time to all computers on the local network
To ensure all local computers have the same newsfeed
To resolve SCADA control issues between compliant devices
explanation: The purpose of an NTP server is to provide the correct time to all computers and devices on a network. A local NTP server can query national servers but does not need to; it can function on its own.
whyWrong: A local NTP server can query national servers, but its purpose is to serve time to local devices.
NTP has nothing to do with newsfeeds.
NTP has nothing to do with SCADA control systems.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 8: Network Services, Review Questions question 13

stem: Company employees have recently started receiving large amounts of spam emails. Which of the following systems can help reduce the amount of spam received? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: Unified threat management (UTM) systems can include antispam capabilities. DMARC is a spam management entry added to DNS zone files as a TXT record.
whyWrong: SCADA refers to industrial control systems, often legacy, and does not filter email.
AAA is authentication, authorization, and accounting, which does not reduce spam.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 8: Network Services, Review Questions question 14

stem: A network administrator is updating features on an AAA server. Which aspect of that server deals specifically with determining which users get to access which network resources?
explanation: Authorization is the set of permissions that decides which resources a user can access. Authentication verifies who the user is, and accounting tracks what they accessed.
whyWrong: Authentication verifies a user's identity rather than deciding which resources they can use.
Accounting tracks or logs who accessed which resource.
Only authorization determines access to resources, so not all three aspects apply.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 8: Network Services, Review Questions question 15

stem: Which type of network service is responsible for collecting and tracking error messages generated by networked devices such as routers?
explanation: A syslog server collects and tracks error messages sent from network devices such as routers. Central logging makes it easier to spot and troubleshoot problems.
whyWrong: AAA handles authentication, authorization, and accounting.
NTP provides time to devices on the network.
UTM is unified threat management, a combined security device.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 8: Network Services, Review Questions question 16

stem: Which of the following is a term that refers to legacy industrial servers that control critical infrastructure?
explanation: Supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems are often legacy systems that control public infrastructure such as power, water, and manufacturing. They are hard to replace, so they often stay in use for decades.
whyWrong: DKIM is a spam management method that signs email with a key pair.
SPF is a spam management method that lists the servers allowed to send a domain's email.
DMARC is a spam management policy for email that fails SPF or DKIM.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 8: Network Services, Review Questions question 17

stem: You just purchased an Alexa smart assistant. What type of service is this?
explanation: Smart assistants are examples of Internet of Things (IoT) devices. IoT devices are everyday things that connect to the network and the Internet, such as speakers, thermostats, and cameras.
whyWrong: UTM is unified threat management, which is a security service.
SCADA refers to industrial control systems, often legacy hardware and software.
AAA is authentication, authorization, and accounting.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 8: Network Services, Review Questions question 19

stem: What type of firewall can perform URL filtering, content filtering, and malware inspection?
explanation: A unified threat management (UTM) appliance combines several security functions in one device, such as a firewall, URL filtering, content filtering, malware inspection, and intrusion prevention. It is managed from one console, which suits small and medium networks.
whyWrong: A stateless firewall only filters packets by addresses, ports, and protocols.
A host-based firewall runs on one computer and only filters that computer's traffic.
A stateful firewall tracks connection states but does not by itself filter URLs or inspect for malware.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.2 question 3
note: Old 220-1101 2.2 (networking hardware); UTM is now under 220-1201 2.3 Internet appliances.

stem: The helpdesk has been overwhelmed by network users saying that they cannot access any network resources. What server should the helpdesk ensure is up and running?
explanation: When many users cannot reach any network resource, the DHCP server is a likely cause: without it, clients get no IP address and fall back to APIPA addresses. The helpdesk should check that the DHCP server is running.
whyWrong: A domain controller authenticates users, but an outage would not stop all access to every network resource by IP.
A DNS failure stops name resolution, but users would still have IP connectivity.
A mail server outage only affects email.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.4 question 1

stem: What type of server can provide webpage caching?
explanation: A proxy server makes web requests on behalf of clients and can cache the pages it fetches. Later requests for the same pages are served from the cache, which saves bandwidth and time.
whyWrong: A file server stores and shares documents; it does not cache web pages.
A UTM firewall provides URL filtering, content filtering, and malware inspection rather than page caching.
A web server hosts its own websites; it does not cache other sites' pages for clients.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.4 question 3

stem: What type of network is used in oil or gas refineries?
explanation: Supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) is an industrial control system that monitors and controls plants such as oil and gas refineries, pipelines, and power stations. Many SCADA systems are legacy or embedded systems that are hard to patch.
whyWrong: Production network is not a standard network type.
A local area network connects users and devices in one site; it is not an industrial control system.
A metropolitan area network covers a city; it is not an industrial control system.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.4 question 4

stem: Which of the following could be considered Internet of Things? (Choose two.)
explanation: Internet of Things (IoT) devices are everyday devices that connect to the internet to send data or be controlled, often for home automation. A smart speaker such as Alexa and a smart energy meter both connect to the internet.
whyWrong: A standard alarm clock works on its own with no network connection.
A standard headset connects to one device and does not connect to the internet.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.4 question 5

stem: Which of the following is true about spam gateways? (Select all that apply.)
options: They use SPF, DKIM, and DMARC to verify the authenticity of the mail servers sending emails
They are used to send out spam to other organizations
They use a DLP system to stop PII and other sensitive information from leaving your network
They filter out incoming messages to prevent them from being delivered to users’ mailboxes
explanation: A spam gateway filters incoming email before it reaches users' mailboxes and checks SPF, DKIM, and DMARC to verify the sending servers. Many gateways also apply data loss prevention (DLP) to outgoing mail to stop PII and other sensitive data from leaving.
whyWrong: A spam gateway blocks spam; it is never used to send spam.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.4 question 6

stem: An organization has installed 20 web servers into an existing web array of 30 web servers. How can this array of web servers be optimized for faster response times?
explanation: A load balancer receives incoming client requests and sends each one to the least-busy server in the array. All 50 web servers are then used efficiently, and response times improve.
whyWrong: A cluster gives high availability by failing over between servers; it does not spread requests across a web array.
A proxy server handles outbound client requests and caches pages, not inbound load on web servers.
A DNS server resolves names to IP addresses; it does not balance the load on servers.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.4 question 7

stem: What type of server uses port 25?
explanation: A mail server uses Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) on TCP port 25 to send and relay email. Mail clients use POP3 or IMAP to download their mail.
whyWrong: DNS servers use port 53.
DHCP servers use UDP ports 67 and 68.
Proxy servers commonly use ports such as 8080, not 25.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.4 question 8

stem: What type of content is hosted on a web server?
explanation: A web server hosts websites, each with a home page through which users reach its information and applications. It serves the pages over HTTP or HTTPS.
whyWrong: Stored files for users are kept on a file server.
Mailboxes are kept on a mail server.
Authentication, authorization, and accounting data is handled by an AAA server such as RADIUS.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.4 question 9

stem: A user has a mapped drive that shows a UNC path of \\server1\data. Which of the following network services are they accessing?
explanation: \\server1\data is a UNC path to a shared folder on a server. A mapped drive with this path connects to a file share.
whyWrong: A print server shares printers; its UNC paths point to printer shares, not a data folder for a mapped drive.
A syslog server collects log messages from many devices; it is not reached as a mapped drive.
A proxy server handles web requests for clients; it does not host shared folders.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.4 question 10

stem: Which of the following can authenticate a supplicant without holding a copy of the relevant directory services?
explanation: A RADIUS server is an AAA server that provides authentication, authorization, and accounting. A supplicant is the device that asks for access; the switch, access point, or VPN server passes its request to the RADIUS server, which can check the credentials against a directory without holding its own copy.
whyWrong: A syslog server collects log messages from many devices.
A DNS server resolves host names to IP addresses.
A proxy server makes web requests for clients and caches pages.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.4 question 11
note: Book explanation corrected: it called VPN servers, switches, and access points supplicants; they are the authenticators (RADIUS clients), and the supplicant is the device asking for access.

stem: Which of the following servers centralizes log files from multiple servers?
explanation: A syslog server, also called a log collector, collects and centralizes the log messages of many servers and network devices. Administrators can then search and analyze all logs in one place.
whyWrong: A DHCP server assigns IP addresses to clients.
A file server hosts documents for users.
A domain controller authenticates users in a domain.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.4 question 13

stem: Your system needs to renew its IP address from a DHCP server. What has expired?
explanation: The IP lease has expired. When this happens, the client needs to renew the address or seek a new one from another DHCP server.
whyWrong: An IP reservation is an address kept for one server or other special system.
A DHCP scope is the range of IP addresses that a DHCP server assigns to clients.
A MAC address is the unique address written to a network interface card, and it does not expire.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 7: Network Configuration Concepts, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: Which type of DNS record associates an IPv6 address with a hostname?
explanation: An AAAA record associates an IPv6 address with a hostname for forward lookup (name to IP address). The A record does the same for IPv4.
whyWrong: An A record associates an IPv4 address, not an IPv6 address, with a hostname.
The SOA (Start of Authority) record holds the main information about a DNS zone.
An MX (Mail Exchange) record directs email to the proper email server.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 7: Network Configuration Concepts, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: Which of the following is the BEST solution for protecting email domains against spoofing and other unauthorized uses?
explanation: The best listed solution is DMARC, which lets an admin use the SPF or DKIM protocols (or both) in a more secure way. DMARC also sets what receiving servers do with mail that fails the checks and reports on it.
whyWrong: SPF by itself, which lists the servers allowed to send for a domain, is not as functional as DMARC.
DORA is the four-step DHCP process (Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge).
A VLAN is a virtual LAN that organizes and compartmentalizes a LAN, not an email protection.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 7: Network Configuration Concepts, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: You have been tasked with compartmentalizing a network. Which of the following technologies should you use?
explanation: You would create a virtual LAN (VLAN), which splits one physical network into separate logical networks. Another valid option would be to implement IP subnetting.
whyWrong: APIPA (link-local addressing) auto-assigns addresses on the 169.254 network and does not divide a network.
A VPN connects remote clients to a network over the Internet through a secure tunnel.
IPv6 by itself does not compartmentalize a network unless it is also subnetted.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 7: Network Configuration Concepts, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: Which of the following DNS record types directs email to an email server?
explanation: The DNS Mail Exchange (MX) record directs mail to an email server. Each domain that receives mail needs at least one MX record.
whyWrong: An A record stores the IPv4 address of a domain or host for forward lookup.
An AAAA record stores the IPv6 address of a domain or host.
A TXT record holds administrative text notes and is used by email authentication methods such as SPF.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 7: Network Configuration Concepts, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: Why would a network administrator configure DHCP exclusions within a DHCP scope?
options: To ensure specific IP addresses are not dynamically assigned, typically because they are reserved for devices with static IPs
To prevent DHCP servers from responding to requests from unauthorized MAC addresses
To block specific clients from obtaining any IP address through DHCP
To permanently assign the same IP address to a client using its MAC address
explanation: DHCP exclusions keep specific IP addresses within the scope from being handed out dynamically. This prevents conflicts with devices that are assigned static IPs manually, such as servers, printers, or firewalls.
whyWrong: Ignoring requests from unauthorized MAC addresses is done with MAC filtering or network access control, not exclusions.
Blocking specific clients from getting any address needs access control or DHCP deny lists, not exclusions.
Permanently assigning the same IP address to a client by its MAC address is a DHCP reservation, not an exclusion.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 89

stem: Which of the following networking hardware devices is capable of creating VLANs?
explanation: A managed switch can create virtual LANs (VLANs) using its management software. Unmanaged switches have no configuration options, so they cannot divide ports into VLANs.
whyWrong: A firewall is a hardware or software solution that filters traffic, not a device that creates VLANs.
A patch panel is a passive termination point for cable runs and cannot create VLANs.
An unmanaged switch has no configuration interface, so it cannot create VLANs.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 6: Networking Fundamentals, Review Questions question 9

stem: You are setting up clients to use the new corporate VPN. The VPN will encrypt all data in transit between employees who work from home and the corporate office. Which protocol will secure the VPN?
explanation: IPSec works at OSI Layer 3, so it can encrypt all traffic that passes between the remote employees and the corporate office. That makes it the protocol listed here that secures the whole VPN tunnel.
whyWrong: HTTPS secures web sessions between a browser and a web server, not all traffic in a VPN.
TLS secures individual application sessions, such as HTTPS, rather than all IP traffic in this design.
SSL is the older, insecure predecessor of TLS and secures application sessions, not the whole tunnel.
