source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 7: Introduction to TCP/IP, Review Questions question 1
note: IPSec is not named in the 220-1201 objectives; tagged to VPN (2.4).

stem: Which of the following solutions can help reduce broadcast traffic received by TCP/IP-based computers on a network?
explanation: A VLAN is a virtual LAN configured on a switch. It breaks a network into smaller logical broadcast domains, which reduces the number of broadcasts each computer receives.
whyWrong: DNS resolves hostnames to IP addresses and does not limit broadcasts.
DHCP assigns IP configuration information and actually relies on broadcasts.
A VPN is a secure connection over a public network and does not divide a LAN into broadcast domains.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 7: Introduction to TCP/IP, Review Questions question 10

stem: Which of the following is the name of a secure point-to-point connection made over a public network?
explanation: A virtual private network (VPN) is a secure point-to-point connection made over a public network. It encrypts the traffic in a tunnel so remote users can reach private resources safely.
whyWrong: NAT translates private IP addresses to public IP addresses.
APIPA assigns an address automatically when a client cannot reach a DHCP server.
A VLAN is a virtual local area network configured on switches.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 7: Introduction to TCP/IP, Review Questions question 16

stem: What does a DHCP server need to be configured with to operate properly?
explanation: Every DHCP server needs a scope, which is the range of addresses available to clients, along with other options that it can give to client computers. Without a scope, the server has nothing to lease.
whyWrong: A DHCP server can optionally give clients a DNS server address, but it is not required to operate.
DHCP has no separate setting called a range; the address range is part of the scope.
A DHCP relay agent forwards DHCP requests from a subnet with no DHCP server and is not required on the server.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 8: Network Services, Review Questions question 6

stem: When configuring a DNS server, administrators must create which of the following?
explanation: DNS server records are contained in the zone file, which administrators must configure. The zone file holds records such as A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, and TXT.
whyWrong: A hosts file is a local alternative to DNS that does not scale to the Internet.
A scope is created on DHCP servers, not DNS servers.
There is no DNS proxy that administrators must create.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 8: Network Services, Review Questions question 7

stem: You are configuring a DHCP server for a small network with a network address of 192.168.1.0/24. You want the DHCP server to manage and assign all IP addresses and also want to ensure that there are 20 addresses available for servers, printers, and router interfaces. Which of the following is the BEST solution?
options: Create a scope with addresses 192.168.1.1 to 192.168.1.200. Create an exclusion for addresses 192.168.1.1 to 192.168.1.20.
Create a scope with addresses 192.168.1.1 to 192.168.1.200. Create a lease for addresses 192.168.1.1 to 192.168.1.20.
Create a scope with addresses 192.168.1.21 to 192.168.1.200. Create an inclusion for addresses 192.168.1.1 to 192.168.1.20.
Create a scope with addresses 192.168.1.1 to 192.168.1.200. Create reservations for addresses 192.168.1.1 to 192.168.1.20.
explanation: The best answer is to create a scope with the addresses that the server will manage. Then, to make the server give the same address each time to servers, printers, and router interfaces, create reservations for those addresses.
whyWrong: An exclusion would keep those addresses out of DHCP, so you would have to assign them by hand and the server would not manage all addresses.
A lease is the temporary assignment a client receives, not a setting that sets addresses aside for specific devices.
DHCP has no inclusion setting, and this scope leaves the first 20 addresses unmanaged.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 8: Network Services, Review Questions question 11

stem: You're adding entries for new servers into the corporate DNS server and have IPv6 addresses for those servers. Which type of entries will you create?
explanation: IPv6 hosts have AAAA records in a DNS zone file. IPv4 hosts have A records.
whyWrong: An A record maps a hostname to an IPv4 address, not an IPv6 address.
A CNAME record is an alias that points one name to another.
A TXT record holds text, such as spam management data.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 8: Network Services, Review Questions question 12

stem: Your company has decided to set up its own DHCP server. How many DHCP servers is the company required to maintain?
options: It depends on how many computers are on the network.
explanation: A company that implements DHCP needs only one DHCP server. Having more than one can cause administrative headaches if the servers are not configured properly.
whyWrong: Two DHCP servers are not required, although some networks add one for redundancy.
Three DHCP servers are not required.
One DHCP server can serve a network of any common size, so the count does not depend on the number of computers.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 8: Network Services, Review Questions question 18

stem: Which spam management capability authenticates email servers based on their IP addresses?
explanation: Sender Policy Framework (SPF) is the simplest of the three DNS TXT record types for spam management. It authenticates mail servers based on their IP address.
whyWrong: DKIM authenticates mail with a public-private key pair, not by IP address.
DMARC tells receivers what to do with email that fails SPF or DKIM checks.
SCADA refers to industrial control systems, not spam management.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 8: Network Services, Review Questions question 20

stem: If a home user has an internet connection but cannot connect to any websites and reports this to their ISP, what should the system administrator of the ISP check FIRST?
options: The IP address of the user’s device
explanation: When a user has an internet connection but cannot reach any website by name, name resolution is failing. The ISP should check the DNS server settings FIRST.
whyWrong: The user is already connected to the internet, so the login credentials are working.
The device has internet connectivity, so its IP address is working.
All websites fail, so the problem is not with particular destination web servers.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.4 question 2

stem: The financial director of an enterprise raised a ticket as they were unable to connect to any network resources. What should the system administrator check FIRST?
explanation: A user who cannot connect to any network resource most likely has no IP address from DHCP and an APIPA address instead. The administrator should FIRST check that the DHCP server has assigned the user an address.
whyWrong: SNMP monitors and reports on network devices; it does not give users access to resources.
A RADIUS server authenticates network access, but a problem with it would not be the first thing to check for one user's loss of all resources.
A DNS failure stops name resolution, but the user would still reach resources by IP address.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.6 question 1

stem: What DNS record needs to be allocated to a host with an IP address of 2001:0436:2CA1:0057:0023:0567:5673:0005?
explanation: The address is an IPv6 address, so the host needs an AAAA record, which maps a host name to an IPv6 address. An A record maps a name to an IPv4 address.
whyWrong: An A record maps a name to an IPv4 address, not IPv6.
An MX record names the mail server for a domain.
A TXT record holds free-form text such as SPF, DKIM, or DMARC data.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.6 question 2
note: Book option "AAA" corrected to AAAA, the IPv6 host record.

stem: What is the default lease duration of a Microsoft DHCP server?
explanation: A Microsoft DHCP server gives leases of 8 days by default. The client tries to renew the lease when half of the lease time has passed.
whyWrong: 12 days is not the default lease time of a Microsoft DHCP server.
14 days is not the default lease time of a Microsoft DHCP server.
2 days is not the default lease time of a Microsoft DHCP server.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.6 question 3

stem: Users in a small company cannot access the mail server on Monday morning. The system administrator had migrated the old mail server to a new version but did not update the DNS record for the mail server. What DNS records do they need to update?
explanation: A mail exchanger (MX) record tells other mail servers which server receives email for the domain. After a mail server migration, the MX record must point to the new mail server.
whyWrong: An A record maps a host name to an IPv4 address; it does not say which server handles the domain's mail.
An AAAA record maps a host name to an IPv6 address; it does not say which server handles the domain's mail.
SRV records locate services such as domain controllers.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.6 question 4
note: Book option "AAA" corrected to AAAA.

stem: Which of the following uses cryptography to confirm that the source server that an email came from was legitimate?
explanation: With DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM), the sending server signs each message, and the domain publishes its public key in a DNS TXT record. Receiving servers use the key to check that the message came from an authorized server.
whyWrong: SPF lists the servers allowed to send mail for a domain, but it uses no cryptographic signature.
DMARC tells receivers what to do with mail that fails SPF or DKIM checks; it does not sign messages itself.
A syslog server collects log messages from many systems.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.6 question 6

stem: One of the users in a company keeps raising support tickets for very minor issues. The IT team wants to be able to track him by his IP address. The company is using a DHCP server to dynamically allocate IP addresses. How can the IT team set this user up so that he gets the same IP address from the DHCP server?
options: Create a new scope for him
Create a customized lease duration for him
Create a static IP address for him
explanation: A DHCP reservation ties an IP address to a host's MAC address, so the DHCP server always gives that host the same address. The host still gets its settings from DHCP.
whyWrong: A scope is the range of addresses for a whole subnet, not a fixed address for one host.
A different lease duration does not make DHCP give the same address each time.
A static address is set by hand on the host and does not come from the DHCP server.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.6 question 7

stem: Which of the following technologies allows multiple networks to be created within a switch?
explanation: A virtual LAN (VLAN) divides one physical switch into several logical networks, each its own broadcast domain. VLANs are used to isolate departments or types of traffic.
whyWrong: A proxy server makes web requests for internal clients; it does not create networks in a switch.
A firewall filters traffic between networks; it does not create networks in a switch.
A router connects separate networks rather than dividing a switch into networks.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.6 question 8

stem: The spam gateway was fooled by spam coming from many different fake domains. Which of the following can be implemented to prevent these emails from accessing the company network?
explanation: Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance (DMARC) builds on SPF and DKIM to validate incoming mail and detect spoofed senders. Messages that fail the checks can be rejected or quarantined.
whyWrong: A firewall filters traffic by rules; it does not check whether an email's sending domain is genuine.
A content filter blocks inappropriate web content; it does not authenticate email senders.
A proxy server handles outgoing web requests; it does not check incoming email.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.6 question 9

stem: A network administrator is planning to divide the company’s network into three subnets. What do they need to configure in the DHCP server so that each subnet gets a certain range of IP addresses that are unique to that subnet?
explanation: A DHCP scope is the range of IP addresses that the DHCP server can give out on one subnet, with its settings such as the gateway. Three subnets need three scopes.
whyWrong: A reservation always gives one host the same address; it does not set a subnet's range.
A lease is the length of time a host may use its address.
A superscope groups several scopes so they act as one; it does not give each subnet its own range.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.6 question 10

stem: What is the DNS record used by a host with an IP address of 131.122.14.12?
explanation: 131.122.14.12 is an IPv4 address, so the host uses an A record. AAAA records are for IPv6 addresses.
whyWrong: An AAAA record maps a name to an IPv6 address.
An MX record names the mail server for a domain.
An SPF record (a TXT record) lists the servers allowed to send mail for a domain.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.6 question 11
note: Book option "AAA" corrected to AAAA.

stem: What is the sequence of the DHCP handshake?
explanation: The DHCP process is DISCOVER, OFFER, REQUEST, ACK (DORA). The client broadcasts a DHCPDISCOVER, the server replies with a DHCPOFFER of an address and settings, the client sends a DHCPREQUEST for it, and the server confirms with a DHCPACK and the lease.
whyWrong: The process cannot start with an ACK; the client starts it with a DISCOVER.
The client can only request an address after a server has offered one.
The client cannot request an address before it has discovered a server.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.6 question 12

stem: Which of the following is a method that can be used to securely connect a remote user’s laptop to a corporate server from overseas?
explanation: A virtual private network (VPN) creates an encrypted tunnel over the internet between the remote laptop and the corporate network. The user can then reach corporate servers securely from anywhere.
whyWrong: A WAN is a network over a large area, such as the internet itself; it does not secure the connection.
SSL encrypts traffic for a web session but does not by itself connect the laptop to the corporate network.
DHCP assigns IP addresses to hosts.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.6 question 13

stem: Which of the following tools can be used to prevent spear phishing or spam attacks? (Select all that apply.)
explanation: SPF records in DNS list the servers allowed to send mail for a domain, and DKIM uses cryptographic signatures to prove a message came from an authorized server. DMARC builds on both to detect and block spoofed email, which helps stop spam and spear phishing.
whyWrong: A stateless firewall filters packets by address and port and cannot check email senders.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.6 question 14

stem: Which of the following technologies would allow a network host to be allocated an IP address based on its MAC address?
explanation: A DHCP server assigns IP addresses automatically, and a DHCP reservation gives one host the same address every time based on its MAC address. This makes the host easy to identify and monitor.
whyWrong: SMTP sends email; it does not assign IP addresses.
SSL encrypts data in transit, such as web sessions.
DNS resolves host names to IP addresses; it does not assign addresses.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.7 question 7
note: Old 220-1101 2.7 set; the content matches 220-1201 2.4 DHCP reservations.

stem: How can a printer in a SOHO obtain the same IP from a wireless router running DHCP?
options: Configure a static IP address for the printer
Use a USB cable for network connectivity
explanation: A DHCP reservation links an IP address to the printer's MAC address, so the DHCP server always gives the printer the same IP address. Clients can then always find the printer at that address.
whyWrong: A static IP address is set on the printer itself and does not come from the DHCP server.
Restarting the router does not make DHCP give the same address each time.
A USB cable connects the printer to one computer and gives it no IP address.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.6 question 13
note: Old objective 220-1101 3.6 (printers and MFDs).

stem: When remotely accessing the company network, which option provides a secure connection to the company LAN?
explanation: A virtual private network (VPN) creates an encrypted tunnel between the remote device and the company LAN. This keeps the data private and secure during remote access.
whyWrong: A faster internet connection does not encrypt or secure the traffic.
A public IP address makes a device reachable from the internet; it does not secure the connection.
A firewall filters traffic but does not create a secure tunnel to the company LAN.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.7 question 6
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.7 (network troubleshooting) = current 5.5. Tagged to current 2.4 VPN.

stem: Which of the following is most often used to connect a group of computers in a LAN? (Select all that apply.)
explanation: Computers in a LAN are connected by a central connecting device, most commonly a switch or a wireless access point (WAP). The ports on the back of a SOHO router are really its built-in switch; the router function is the link between the LAN and the Internet.
whyWrong: A router is designed to connect two networks, not the computers inside one LAN.
A bridge connects two LANs or separates one LAN into two sections.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 8: Network Devices, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: What device protects a network from unwanted intrusion?
explanation: A firewall is a hardware appliance or software application that protects one or more computers from unwanted intrusion. It does this by blocking ports and protocols.
whyWrong: A switch connects multiple computers together on a LAN.
A router connects two or more networks.
An access point lets Wi-Fi devices communicate on the LAN wirelessly.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 8: Network Devices, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: Which of the following network devices moves frames of data between a source and destination, based on their MAC addresses?
explanation: A switch sends frames of data between computers by identifying the systems by their MAC addresses. It forwards each frame only to the port of the destination system.
whyWrong: A hub broadcasts data out to all computers, and only the intended computer accepts it.
A router moves packets between networks by IP address, such as from the LAN to the Internet.
A modem converts a computer's digital signals for transmission over a line such as a phone or cable line.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 8: Network Devices, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: Which of the following network devices allows a remote device to obtain Ethernet data as well as electrical power?
explanation: A Power over Ethernet (PoE) injector sends Ethernet data and power over a single twisted pair cable to a remote device. The device that receives the power is called the powered device (PD).
whyWrong: A PD (powered device) is the PoE device that receives the power, not the one that supplies it.
A firewall secures ports on a network or on an individual system.
A router connects one network to another, such as the LAN to the Internet.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 8: Network Devices, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: Which of the following devices can be configured when accessed from a browser or SSH or similar configuration tool?
explanation: Managed switches can be configured from a browser, SSH, or a similar tool. For example, you can change the device's IP address, configure ports, and monitor the switch and other devices with SNMP.
whyWrong: An unmanaged switch has no configuration interface; it simply connects devices on the Ethernet network.
A patch panel is a passive termination point for the network cables in a building.
A network interface card connects a computer to a network and is not configured as a network device.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 8: Network Devices, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: Which of the following acts as a demarcation point for fiber optic services?
explanation: An optical network terminal (ONT) is a network interface device that takes the incoming fiber optic line from a provider and splits it off to the customer's premises for Internet access, voice, and television. The cables from the ONT into the premises are often copper (coaxial or twisted pair).
whyWrong: Software-defined networking (SDN) administers multiple network devices with a controller program.
A patch panel terminates twisted pair cables on one side and has ports for patch cables on the other.
A NIC is an adapter card that lets a PC access a wired network; do not confuse it with a NID.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 8: Network Devices, Cram Quiz question 6

stem: Which of the following is an example of a MAC address?
explanation: 00-1C-C0-A1-55-21 is a MAC address, the address burned into a network adapter that uniquely identifies it. It is six hexadecimal numbers from 00 to FF; the first three are the OUI (here an Intel OUI) and the last three identify the adapter. MAC addresses can also be separated by colons instead of hyphens.
whyWrong: 10.1.1.255 is an IPv4 address.
4410:FF11:AAB3::0012 is a truncated IPv6 address.
https://greencurtaintraining.com is a web address (URL) with a protocol and a domain name.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 13

stem: Which of the following devices should be configured to block specific ports on a network?
explanation: The firewall is the device that prevents outside intrusion by blocking ports and protocols. In many networks it is the first line of defense.
whyWrong: A gateway, usually a router, lets clients on one network reach another network.
A router connects two networks together.
A bridge separates a LAN into two network sections.
An access point gives Wi-Fi devices wireless access to the network.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 43

stem: Which of the following describes the function of a switch in a network?
options: Converts a packet for transmission from one network to another network
Transmits packets it receives to specific connections (ports)
Broadcasts packets it receives to all connections
Determines whether a packet belongs on an internal or an external network
explanation: A switch transmits the packets it receives to specific connections (ports). It does this by mapping systems' MAC addresses to its physical ports.
whyWrong: Converting a packet for transmission from one network to another is the job of a router.
A hub, not a switch, broadcasts packets it receives to all connections.
A router determines whether a packet belongs on an internal or an external network.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 53

stem: What devices transfer packets across multiple networks and use tables to store network addresses to determine the best destination?
explanation: Routers are designed to route (transfer) packets across networks. They determine the best path to take based on the internal routing tables that they maintain.
whyWrong: A firewall filters traffic with rules; it does not choose paths between networks with routing tables.
A hub repeats every signal out of all its ports and keeps no address tables.
A switch forwards frames within one network using MAC addresses, not between networks.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 6: Networking Fundamentals, Review Questions question 8

stem: Your ISP has just finished running fiber-optic cable in your neighborhood, and you want to switch from cable Internet to a faster fiber-optic connection. Which of the following statements is true about how you will get an Internet connection?
options: You will continue to use your cable modem.
You need to switch to using a DSL modem.
You need to switch to using an ONT.
You need to switch to using PoE.
explanation: Fiber-optic Internet connections use an optical network terminal (ONT) to terminate the fiber and translate it into a digital connection over copper cable inside your home. A cable modem and a DSL modem connect copper to copper, so neither can terminate fiber.
whyWrong: A cable modem works with the provider's coaxial cable, not with a fiber-optic line.
A DSL modem works over telephone copper lines, not fiber.
Power over Ethernet delivers power to devices over network cable and has nothing to do with terminating a fiber connection.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 6: Networking Fundamentals, Review Questions question 11

stem: What type of device will block unwanted traffic from your network using a set of rules called an ACL?
explanation: The job of a firewall is to block unwanted network traffic. Firewalls do this by using a list of rules called an access control list (ACL).
whyWrong: A router connects networks to each other and forwards packets between them.
A switch is a central connectivity point that forwards frames inside a network.
A network attached storage (NAS) device is a dedicated file storage device, not a traffic filter.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 6: Networking Fundamentals, Review Questions question 17

stem: Which type of device works with MAC addresses to determine what to do with network traffic?
explanation: A switch works at Layer 2, so it uses hardware (MAC) addresses to decide which port should receive each frame. It learns the MAC address of each connected NIC and keeps them in a table.
whyWrong: A hub works at Layer 1 and repeats bits out of every port without reading addresses.
A router works at Layer 3 and makes its decisions with logical IP addresses.
A patch panel is a passive Layer 1 device that only connects cable runs.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 6: Networking Fundamentals, Review Questions question 19

stem: Which of the following protocols is responsible for resolving IP addresses to hardware addresses?
explanation: The Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) resolves IP addresses to hardware (MAC) addresses. Each NIC has a physical MAC address, and ARP finds the MAC address that belongs to a given IP address on the local network.
whyWrong: DNS resolves hostnames to IP addresses, not IP addresses to MAC addresses.
DHCP automatically configures TCP/IP clients.
RARP does the reverse: it resolves MAC addresses to IP addresses.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 7: Introduction to TCP/IP, Review Questions question 20
note: ARP is not named in the 220-1201 objectives; tagged to NIC MAC address (2.5).

stem: A firewall operates by using a set of rules known as what?
explanation: The set of access rules on a firewall is called an access control list (ACL). Each rule allows or denies traffic based on items such as address, port, and protocol.
whyWrong: A service level agreement (SLA) is a contract about the level of service, not a set of firewall rules.
NAT translates private IP addresses into public ones.
APIPA assigns an IP address to a client that cannot reach a DHCP server.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 9: Wireless and SOHO Networking, Review Questions question 17

stem: How many bits are in a MAC address?
explanation: MAC addresses are 48 bits long. They are usually written as 12 hexadecimal digits, and the first half identifies the NIC manufacturer.
whyWrong: 24 bits is only the manufacturer half (the OUI) of a MAC address.
36 bits is not the length of a MAC address.
64 bits is the length of the interface ID in an IPv6 address, not of a standard MAC address.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 18: Essentials of Networking, Chapter Review question 1

stem: What kind of frame gets received by all NICs in a LAN?
explanation: All NICs in a LAN receive broadcast frames. A broadcast frame is addressed to FF-FF-FF-FF-FF-FF, so a switch forwards it out every port.
whyWrong: Cat 7 is a cable category, not a kind of frame.
A WAN is a network type that spans large distances, not a frame.
SC, ST, and LC are fiber optic connectors, not frames.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 18: Essentials of Networking, Chapter Review question 6
note: All-in-One 11e (220-1101/1102) Ch. 18: broadcast frames are not listed by name; closest topic is Switches.

stem: You are down under your desk organizing some wires when you notice that the activity light on your NIC is blinking erratically. Is there a problem?
options: Yes, the activity light should be on steadily when the computer is running.
Yes, the activity light should be blinking steadily, not randomly.
No, the light blinks when there is network traffic.
No, the light blinks to show bus activity.
explanation: The activity light blinks to show network traffic, so erratic blinking is normal. Traffic comes and goes at irregular intervals, and the light follows it.
whyWrong: A steady light is a link light showing a connection, not the activity light.
Network traffic is not regular, so the activity light does not blink at a steady rate.
The NIC's activity light shows network traffic, not traffic on the computer's internal bus.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 19: Local Area Networking, Chapter Review question 6
note: All-in-One 11e (220-1101/1102) Ch. 19: NIC status lights are not listed by name; closest topic is Network interface card (NIC).

stem: What benefit does full-duplex offer?
options: It enables NICs to send and receive signals at the same time.
It enables NICs to send data twice as fast.
It enables NICs to receive data twice as fast.
It enables a switch to connect to both coaxial and fiber optic cables.
explanation: Full-duplex technology enables NICs to send and receive signals at the same time. A half-duplex NIC must take turns sending and receiving.
whyWrong: Full-duplex does not change the sending speed; it lets sending and receiving happen at once.
Full-duplex does not double the receiving speed of a single direction.
Duplex mode has nothing to do with connecting coaxial and fiber cables.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 19: Local Area Networking, Chapter Review question 9
note: All-in-One 11e (220-1101/1102) Ch. 19: duplex is not listed by name; closest topic is Network interface card (NIC).

stem: Which device creates a wireless network?
explanation: A wireless access point (WAP) enables clients to join a wireless network. It sends out the network's signal and connects the wireless clients to the wired network.
whyWrong: A wireless extender extends the range of an existing network but does not create one.
Wireless locator is not a device that creates a network.
A wireless repeater only repeats an existing network's signal to extend its range.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 20: Wireless Networking, Chapter Review question 3

stem: Which type of wireless network hardware automatically works with its peers to forward traffic?
explanation: In wireless mesh networks, each network device can forward traffic for the others, while one of the devices serves as the gateway. Mesh nodes work together automatically to cover a large area with one network.
whyWrong: A standard access point serves its own clients and does not forward traffic for peer devices.
A wireless repeater only rebroadcasts one access point's signal.
A wireless extender only extends one network's range and does not cooperate with peers.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 20: Wireless Networking, Chapter Review question 4
note: All-in-One 11e (220-1101/1102) Ch. 20: mesh networks are not listed by name; closest topic is Access points.

stem: What determines the name of a wireless network?
explanation: The service set identifier (SSID) determines the name of a wireless network. The access point broadcasts the SSID so clients can find and join the network.
whyWrong: EAP is an authentication framework, not a network name.
A MAC address identifies one network interface, not the wireless network.
A WAP is the device that creates the network, not its name.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 20: Wireless Networking, Chapter Review question 5
note: All-in-One 11e (220-1101/1102) Ch. 20: the SSID is not listed under 2.5; closest topic is Access points. SSID security settings are 220-1202 2.10.

stem: What is the name for the common omni-directional antennas found on wireless access points?
explanation: Standard omni-directional antennas are called dipole antennas. They look like a stick but contain two antenna arms aligned on the antenna's axis, and they send the signal evenly in all directions.
whyWrong: Bipole antenna is not the name of the standard access point antenna.
Omni-directional describes the coverage pattern, not the name of the antenna type.
RF (radio frequency) describes every wireless antenna, not this type.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 20: Wireless Networking, Chapter Review question 9
note: All-in-One 11e (220-1101/1102) Ch. 20: antenna types are not listed under 2.5; closest topic is Access points.

stem: A junior network administrator has been asked to identify the front and back of a patch panel. Which of the following are true? (Choose two.)
options: The front of the patch panel is where cabling running through the company terminates at the insulation displacement connector (IDC)
The back of the patch panel is where cabling running through the company terminates at the insulation displacement connector (IDC)
The front of the patch panel has prewired RJ45 ports
The back of the patch panel has prewired RJ45 ports
explanation: The back of a patch panel is where the cable runs from the building terminate on insulation displacement connector (IDC) blocks, using a punchdown tool. The front has prewired RJ45 ports for short patch cables to the switch.
whyWrong: The front of the patch panel has the RJ45 ports; the IDC terminations are on the back.
The back of the patch panel has the IDC blocks, not the RJ45 ports.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.2 question 1

stem: What is the purpose of an Optical Network Terminal (ONT) installed at a customer’s home?
options: It provides fiber to the curb (FTTC)
The ONT converts optical signals to electrical signals
The ONT converts electrical signals and converts them to optical signals
The ONT is located in a street cabinet
explanation: An optical network terminal (ONT) at the customer premises ends the provider's fiber line and converts the optical signals to electrical signals for the customer's router and devices. It is used with fiber to the premises.
whyWrong: Fiber to the curb runs the fiber to a cabinet near the homes; an ONT is the device at the end of a fiber line in the home.
Converting from electrical to optical is the reverse of the ONT's job for the incoming signal.
The ONT is installed at the customer premises, not in a street cabinet.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.2 question 4

stem: Which of the following allows a host to pull power for a device through an ethernet cable plugged into a switch?
explanation: Power over Ethernet (PoE) carries power over the Ethernet cable from a PoE switch or injector. Devices such as access points, IP phones, and cameras then need no separate power adapter.
whyWrong: Thunderbolt is a high-speed peripheral and display interface, not a way to power devices from a switch.
A managed switch can be configured (for example with VLANs), but being managed does not mean it supplies power.
Shielded twisted pair adds foil shielding against EMI; it does not supply power by itself.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.2 question 5

stem: Which of the following network devices can be used to reduce the size of broadcast domains in a LAN? (Choose two.)
explanation: A broadcast stays within its broadcast domain. A router does not forward broadcasts, so each router interface is a separate broadcast domain, and a managed switch can split one LAN into several VLANs, each its own broadcast domain.
whyWrong: A load balancer spreads incoming client requests across several servers; it does not change broadcast domains.
A hub repeats every frame to every port, so all its hosts share one broadcast domain.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.2 question 6
note: Book answer "Load balancer" corrected: the book's own explanation names the managed switch (VLANs), and a router also separates broadcast domains, so the question asks for two answers.

stem: A company wants to use POE as powering switches is more efficient than using an AC adapter and will help reduce the electricity bill. However, two of the switches do not support POE. Bearing in mind that cost is a concern, what can the network engineer do to solve this issue?
explanation: A PoE injector adds power to the Ethernet cable between a non-PoE switch and the powered device. It is cheaper than replacing the switches with PoE-capable ones.
whyWrong: A UPS gives battery backup during a power loss; it does not put power on Ethernet cables.
A generator is a backup power source for outages, not a way to deliver PoE.
New PoE-capable switches would work but cost more than injectors.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.2 question 8

stem: What type of switch is unpacked from the box, turned on, has either 4 or 8 ports, and is used in very small networks?
explanation: An unmanaged switch has no configuration: you take it out of the box, plug it in, and it works. Small models with 4 or 8 ports are common in very small networks.
whyWrong: A managed switch can be configured through a web interface or command line, for example with VLANs.
An aggregation switch combines the traffic of several access switches in a larger network.
A power diode switch is not a type of network switch.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.2 question 9

stem: Which of the following legacy network hardware devices sends any incoming packets it receives to all ports connected to the device?
explanation: A hub is a legacy device that repeats every incoming frame to all of its ports. A switch replaced it because a switch learns MAC addresses and sends each frame only to the port of the destination host.
whyWrong: A load balancer spreads client requests across several servers.
A switch sends a frame only to the port of the destination MAC address, not to every port.
A router connects separate networks and forwards packets by IP address.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.2 question 10
note: Hubs are not in the 220-1201 objectives; the question contrasts the hub with a switch (220-1201 2.5 Switches).

stem: If a network-based firewall is set up to allow HTTP and HTTPS traffic, what happens when a user tries to download a document using FTP?
options: Document will be blocked by its host-based firewall
explanation: A firewall checks traffic against its access control list (ACL) rules in order, and the last rule denies everything that no rule allows. FTP traffic matches no allow rule, so this implicit deny blocks it.
whyWrong: No rule allows FTP, so the firewall blocks the download.
The network-based firewall blocks the traffic before it ever reaches the host.
An explicit deny is a deny rule that the administrator writes; here no rule mentions FTP.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.2 question 11

stem: Which of the following statements about cable modems are true? (Select all that apply.)
options: A cable modem is similar to a DSL router but uses coax
A cable modem is connected to the local router via an RJ45 port
A cable modem accesses the provider’s network via a short segment of coax
The coax used by a cable modem is terminated using threaded F-type connectors
explanation: A cable modem connects to the provider's network over a coaxial cable terminated with threaded F-type connectors. It does the same job as a DSL modem but uses the cable TV network, and it connects to the local router through an RJ45 Ethernet port.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.2 question 12
note: The book gives no explanation; written from the chapter facts.

stem: Which of the following is true concerning a network interface card used with a Cat 5 cable?
options: The NIC card will use a BNC connector
The NIC card will use an RJ45 connector
The NIC card will use an RJ11 connector
The NIC card will run at a speed of 10Mbps
explanation: Cat 5 is twisted pair Ethernet cable, so the NIC uses an RJ45 connector. Cat 5 supports 100 Mbps (Fast Ethernet).
whyWrong: BNC connectors are used with coaxial cable, not twisted pair.
RJ11 connectors are used for telephone lines and dial-up modems.
Cat 5 runs at 100 Mbps; 10 Mbps was the speed of Cat 3 networks.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.2 question 14

stem: What version of Power over Ethernet (POE) can draw power up to 25W?
explanation: IEEE 802.3at (PoE+) delivers up to about 25.5 W to the powered device. 802.3af (PoE) delivers about 13 W, and 802.3bt (PoE++) delivers up to about 51 W (Type 3) or 71 W (Type 4).
whyWrong: 802.11 is the family of wireless LAN standards, not a PoE standard.
802.3bt (PoE++) delivers much more power, up to about 51 W or 71 W.
802.3af (original PoE) delivers only about 13 W to the device.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.2 question 15

stem: Which of the following are true about different types of DSL? (Choose two.)
options: ADSL provides the same upload and download speeds
ADSL provides a fast download but a slow upload speed
The symmetric version of DSL provides a fast upload and a slow download speed
The symmetric version of DSL provides the same upload and download speed
explanation: Asymmetric DSL (ADSL) has a faster download than upload speed, which suits home users who mostly download. Symmetric DSL (SDSL) has the same upload and download speed.
whyWrong: ADSL is asymmetric, so its upload is slower than its download.
Symmetric DSL has equal upload and download speeds.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.2 question 16

stem: If you work from home and need to connect to the internet, which of the following devices are you MOST LIKELY to use?
explanation: A home network connects to the internet through a router, usually a SOHO wireless router that also contains a switch and an access point. The router joins the home network to the ISP's network.
whyWrong: A hub only connects local hosts; it cannot connect a network to the internet.
A switch connects local hosts but does not route traffic to the internet.
A wireless access point only connects wireless devices to the local network; the router provides the internet connection.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.5 question 5
note: Book answer "WAP" corrected to Router: an access point only connects wireless clients to the local network; the internet connection needs a router (SOHO wireless routers combine both).

stem: A network device is not receiving power through the Ethernet connection. What should be done to resolve the issue?
options: Install a Power over Ethernet ( PoE) injector
explanation: A Power over Ethernet (PoE) injector adds power to the Ethernet cable, so a PoE device can get power when the switch port does not supply it. This resolves the power problem for the network device.
whyWrong: Checking the cable connections fixes physical link problems but does not add power to the cable.
Restarting the device does not give it power that the cable does not supply.
Resetting the network settings changes the configuration, not the power supplied over the cable.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.5 question 2
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.5; tagged to current 2.5 Power over Ethernet.

stem: Which of the following is a primary function of a firewall?
explanation: A firewall monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic based on security rules. It allows or denies packets based on factors such as source, destination, port, and protocol.
whyWrong: Data encryption is done by protocols such as TLS or IPsec, not by a firewall's main function.
Virus scanning is done by antivirus software.
User authentication is handled by separate authentication systems.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 18
note: Neil Core 1 mock exam (220-1101).

stem: Which of these addresses needs to be configured to enable a computer access to the Internet or to other networks?
explanation: The gateway address must be configured so that a computer can reach the Internet or other networks through the gateway device. Without it, the computer can talk only to hosts on its own network.
whyWrong: The subnet mask defines the network and host portions of the IP address.
The DNS server address is used for name resolution, not for reaching other networks.
The MAC address is burned into the network adapter by the manufacturer.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 9: SOHO Network Configuration, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: Which technology assigns addresses on the 169.254.0.0 network?
explanation: An address with 169.254 as the first two octets means Automatic Private IP Addressing (APIPA) is in use. This is the link-local range for IPv4, and a client assigns it to itself when it cannot reach a DHCP server.
whyWrong: DHCP assigns IP addresses automatically but does not use the 169.254 network by default.
Static IP addresses are configured manually by the user.
Class B is the range of IP networks with a first octet from 128 through 191.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 9: SOHO Network Configuration, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: You want to test the local loopback IPv6 address. Which address would you use?
explanation: The ::1 address is the local loopback address for IPv6. It works the same way as 127.0.0.1 does for IPv4.
whyWrong: 127.0.0.1 is the IPv4 loopback address, not the IPv6 one.
FE80::/10 is the range of link-local autoconfigured unicast addresses.
::0 is not the loopback address; it only looks like a truncated address with zeros.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 9: SOHO Network Configuration, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: Which of the following IP addresses would you configure so that the computer can take advantage of hostname-to-IP address resolution?
explanation: You would use a DNS server IP address; 8.8.8.8 is a public DNS server run by Google. The DNS server resolves hostnames and domain names to their IP addresses. On some networks, clients use a private DNS address that forwards requests to a DNS server on the Internet.
whyWrong: 127.0.0.1 is the internal loopback address on any system running TCP/IP.
The gateway address gives a system access to the Internet or other networks.
The subnet mask defines the network and host portions of an IP address.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 9: SOHO Network Configuration, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: Of the following, which is a common use for NAT?
options: Defining the network portion of an IPv4 address
Connecting multiple computers using a single public IP address
explanation: Network Address Translation (NAT) converts private IP addresses to public IP addresses. It lets multiple private computers connect through a single public IP address, usually on a router.
whyWrong: The subnet mask defines the network portion of an IPv4 address.
DNS resolves hostnames to IP addresses.
DHCP assigns TCP/IP addresses automatically.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 9: SOHO Network Configuration, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: You are setting up a network for a small office with 30 computers and 1 server. The server will be used as a file sharing device and a print server, and it will act as the domain controller. What kinds of addresses should you assign to the server? (Select the two best answers.)
explanation: Servers are usually assigned static IP addresses instead of addresses from a DHCP server. When you configure TCP/IP manually, you must enter the IP address and a subnet mask, and often a gateway and DNS server address too. A static address does not change, so you can record it in your network documentation.
whyWrong: DHCP is not typically used for servers in a small company.
The MAC address is programmed into the network adapter by the manufacturer and is not normally set by the administrator.
Dynamic IP addresses are handed out to client computers and can change over time.
An FTP address is vague, and the scenario does not mention FTP.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 37

stem: What is the maximum number of IPv6 addresses that can be assigned to one IPv6 interface?
explanation: An IPv6 interface is not limited in the number of addresses that can be assigned, although there could be limits based on practicality. A single interface commonly has a link-local address plus one or more global unicast addresses at the same time.
whyWrong: One interface is not limited to a single unicast address in IPv6.
IPv6 sets no limit of two addresses per interface.
IPv6 sets no limit of three addresses per interface.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 7: Introduction to TCP/IP, Review Questions question 4

stem: Which of the following are valid examples of IPv6 addresses? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: An IPv6 address contains 128 bits, written as eight 16-bit fields of four hexadecimal digits. The first address is written in full, the second is an IPv4 address expressed in IPv6 form, and the third is the first address written in accepted shorthand (leading zeros dropped and one run of zero fields replaced by a double colon).
whyWrong: This address is not valid because the double colon (::) can be used only once within an IPv6 address.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 7: Introduction to TCP/IP, Review Questions question 5

stem: Which of the following IP addresses would not be valid for a DNS server on the Internet?
explanation: On the Internet, a DNS server needs a public IP address. The address 10.25.11.33 is in the private 10.0.0.0 address range, which is not routed on the Internet.
whyWrong: 18.33.66.254 is a public address, so it could be used on the Internet.
155.118.63.11 is a public address, so it could be used on the Internet.
192.186.12.2 is a public address; only 192.168.x.x is in the private 192 range.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 7: Introduction to TCP/IP, Review Questions question 6

stem: The workstations on your network are configured to use a DHCP server. One of the workstations can't communicate with other computers. Its IP address is 169.254.1.18. What could be the problem?
options: It has a private IP address.
It can't reach the DHCP server.
explanation: The address 169.254.1.18 is an APIPA address. Windows clients (and others) configure themselves with an address in the 169.254.0.0 range when they are set to use DHCP but cannot reach a DHCP server.
whyWrong: APIPA also assigns the subnet mask (255.255.0.0), so a wrong mask is not what the address shows.
APIPA addresses are not in the private ranges such as 10.x, 172.16.x, or 192.168.x, and a private address alone would not stop local communication.
APIPA does not assign a default gateway, and a wrong gateway would not produce a 169.254 address.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 7: Introduction to TCP/IP, Review Questions question 7

stem: You are manually configuring a TCP/IP host. Another administrator gives you the router's IP address. What is the TCP/IP term for this?
explanation: The router is your doorway out to other networks, and in TCP/IP terms it is known as the default gateway. Without this setting, the host cannot reach external networks.
whyWrong: The subnet mask tells a host which part of its address is the network, not where the router is.
The DNS server resolves hostnames to IP addresses.
A DHCP server provides IP configuration information to hosts automatically.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 7: Introduction to TCP/IP, Review Questions question 13

stem: Your network is running IPv4. Which of the configuration options are mandatory for your host to communicate on the network? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: The only mandatory IPv4 configuration items are an IP address and a subnet mask. Together they let a host communicate with others on its own network.
whyWrong: A default gateway is needed only to reach other networks, not to communicate on the local network.
A DNS server resolves hostnames to IP addresses, but a host can communicate without one.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 7: Introduction to TCP/IP, Review Questions question 14

stem: Which of the following is an IPv6 broadcast address?
explanation: IPv6 does not have broadcasts. It uses multicasts instead, which are a bit like targeted broadcasts.
whyWrong: ::1 is the IPv6 loopback address used for troubleshooting.
FE80:: is the start of a link-local address.
FF00:: is the start of a multicast address, not a broadcast address.
::FFFF is used as part of an IPv4-mapped address, with the IPv4 address following it.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 7: Introduction to TCP/IP, Review Questions question 18

stem: Which service allows users with private IP addresses to access the Internet using a public IP address?
explanation: Network Address Translation (NAT) lets users with private IP addresses access the Internet with a public IP address. NAT runs on the router and translates each private address to the public address.
whyWrong: DHCP assigns IP configuration information to clients.
DNS resolves hostnames to IP addresses.
DSL is a type of broadband Internet access, not an address translation service.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 9: Wireless and SOHO Networking, Review Questions question 8
note: NAT is not named in the 220-1201 objectives; tagged to private and public IPv4 addresses (2.6).

stem: You are configuring a SOHO client to use TCP/IP. Which parameter is needed to tell the client where to communicate to get on the Internet?
explanation: The gateway, also known as the default gateway, is the address of the router that takes a client to the next network or the Internet. It can be assigned statically or dynamically by a DHCP server.
whyWrong: A static address is a way of assigning an IP address, not the parameter that points to the router.
A dynamic address is assigned by DHCP and does not by itself tell the client where the router is.
APIPA configures a client automatically when no DHCP server answers, and APIPA clients cannot get on the Internet.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 9: Wireless and SOHO Networking, Review Questions question 20

stem: What type of IP address should a server be given?
explanation: A server should have a static IP address that is set manually and never changes, so clients can always find it. Printers and network devices are also given static addresses.
whyWrong: A dynamic address from DHCP can change, so clients could lose track of the server.
An APIPA address is assigned only when a DHCP server cannot be reached, so it is a sign of a fault.
Whether an address is public or private does not decide whether it stays the same.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.5 question 1

stem: What is the limitation of using a private IPv4 address?
options: It can only be used internally
It can only be used for networks of up to 1,000 hosts
It does not have a network ID
It does not have a host ID
explanation: Private IPv4 addresses (10.x.x.x, 172.16-31.x.x, and 192.168.x.x) are not routed on the internet, so they can only be used inside a network. A router with NAT translates them to a public address for internet access.
whyWrong: Private ranges are not limited to 1,000 hosts; the 10.0.0.0 range alone holds over 16 million addresses.
Every IPv4 address, private or public, has a network ID.
Every IPv4 address, private or public, has a host ID.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.5 question 2

stem: A systems administrator is configuring an IP address on the external port of the firewall that connects to the WAN. Which of the following IP addresses will they use?
explanation: The external port that connects to the WAN needs a public IP address, and 131.107.1.1 is the only public address here. Addresses in 10.x.x.x, 172.16-31.x.x, and 192.168.x.x are private, and 169.254.x.x is APIPA.
whyWrong: 192.168.1.1 is a private address that cannot be routed on the internet.
169.254.1.223 is an APIPA address that a host gives itself when it cannot reach a DHCP server.
10.10.15.6 is in the private 10.0.0.0 range.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.5 question 3

stem: Which of the following is the default subnet mask for a Class B IPv4 address?
explanation: A Class B address uses the first two octets for the network ID, so its default subnet mask is 255.255.0.0. Class A uses 255.0.0.0, and Class C uses 255.255.255.0.
whyWrong: 255.0.0.0 is the default subnet mask for a Class A address.
255.255.255.0 is the default subnet mask for a Class C address.
169.254.1.1 is an APIPA host address, not a subnet mask.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.5 question 4

stem: Assuming a subnet mask of 255.255.255.0, which of the following is a valid IPv4 host address?
explanation: With a 255.255.255.0 mask, 212.15.1.2 is a valid host address. An address whose last octet is 0 is the network address, and one whose last octet is 255 is the broadcast address, so neither can be given to a host.
whyWrong: With a 255.255.255.0 mask, 10.1.1.0 is the network address, not a host address.
255.255.255.128 is a subnet mask, not a host address.
With a 255.255.255.0 mask, 12.1.1.255 is the broadcast address, not a host address.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.5 question 6
note: Stem changed: the book asked for a "valid IPv4 address" without a mask, but with the default Class A mask 10.1.1.0 and 12.1.1.255 are valid host addresses; the /24 mask makes the book's answer the only one.

stem: A Windows server has been configured with both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses. What is this known as?
explanation: A host that runs IPv4 and IPv6 at the same time is called dual stack. It can talk to both IPv4 and IPv6 networks.
whyWrong: Double stack is not the name for this configuration.
Double IP addressing is not the name for this configuration.
Dual IP addressing is not the standard name; the term is dual stack.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.5 question 7

stem: Which of the following are reasons why a desktop might be allocated an IP address of 169.254.11.2? (Select all that apply.)
options: The desktop might have a bad cable or cannot send its broadcast to the DHCP server
The desktop might not be able to contact a DNS server
The desktop might not be able to connect to a domain controller
The desktop might have been allocated a duplicate IP address
explanation: A host gives itself an APIPA address (169.254.x.x) when it cannot get an address from a DHCP server, most often because of a bad cable or no connection to the DHCP server. Windows can also fall back to APIPA when the address it was offered is already in use on the network.
whyWrong: DNS resolves names after the host has an address; a DNS failure does not cause an APIPA address.
A domain controller handles authentication; failing to reach it does not cause an APIPA address.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.5 question 8

stem:
A user is unable to access the internet. When the system administrator runs the ipconfig /all command, they get the following output:
IPv4 Address. . . . . . . . . . . : 132.24.0.1
Subnet Mask . . . . . . . . . . . : 255.255.0.0
Default Gateway . . . . . . . . . :
Which of the following is the source of this problem?
explanation: The output has no default gateway, so the computer cannot send traffic outside its own network, including to the internet. A default gateway is required for internet access.
whyWrong: DNS might matter once the host can leave the network, but the missing gateway stops all internet traffic first.
132.24.0.1 is a public address, not a private one.
Whether the address is dynamic or static does not stop internet access; the missing gateway does.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.5 question 9

stem: How many bits does an IPv4 address use?
explanation: An IPv4 address has four octets of 8 bits each, so it is 32 bits long. IPv6 addresses are 128 bits.
whyWrong: 8 bits is the size of one octet, not of a whole IPv4 address.
16 bits is two octets, half of an IPv4 address.
64 bits is the size of the interface ID in an IPv6 address.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.5 question 10

stem: Which of the following is an IPv6 address?
explanation: 2001:0dC8:0000:0000:0abc:0000:def0:2311 is an IPv6 address: eight groups of four hexadecimal digits separated by colons, 128 bits in all. IPv4 addresses use four decimal numbers separated by dots.
whyWrong: 10.1.1.1 is a private IPv4 address.
B4-2E-99-C0-75-45 is a MAC address.
169.254.1.5 is an IPv4 APIPA address that a host gives itself when it cannot reach a DHCP server.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.5 question 11

stem: How can you shorten the following IPv6 address: 2001:0dC8:0000:0000:0abc:0000:def0:2311?
explanation: To shorten an IPv6 address, remove the leading zeros in each group, so 0dC8 becomes dC8 and 0abc becomes abc. Replace one run of all-zero groups with ::, here the third and fourth groups. The sixth group is also 0000, but :: can be used only once, so it becomes 0, giving 2001:dC8::abc:0:def0:2311.
whyWrong: The double colon appears twice, so the number of missing zero groups is ambiguous and the address is invalid.
The leading zeros are not removed and the zero group 0000 is left after the double colon, so the address is not fully shortened.
It uses the double colon twice and drops a trailing zero from def0, which changes the address.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.5 question 13

stem: Which of the following is a public IPv4 address?
explanation: 126.1.1.1 is a public IPv4 address. The private ranges are 10.0.0.0/8, 172.16.0.0-172.31.255.255, and 192.168.0.0/16, and every unicast address outside them (and outside reserved ranges such as APIPA and loopback) is public.
whyWrong: 10.10.10.1 is in the private 10.0.0.0 range.
192.168.5.6 is in the private 192.168.0.0 range.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.5 question 14

stem: How many bits does an IPv6 address use?
explanation: An IPv6 address is 128 bits long, usually 64 bits for the network prefix and 64 bits for the interface ID. IPv4 addresses are 32 bits.
whyWrong: 16 bits is the size of one group of an IPv6 address.
32 bits is the size of an IPv4 address.
64 bits is only the interface ID or the network prefix of an IPv6 address.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.5 question 15

stem: What is the primary purpose of Network Address Translation (NAT) in networking?
options: To encrypt network traffic for secure communication
To translate domain names into IP addresses
To assign unique IP addresses to each device on a network
To map private IP addresses to public IP addresses
explanation: Network Address Translation (NAT) lets many devices on a private network share one public IP address. The router translates the devices' private addresses to its public address so that they can communicate with devices on the internet.
whyWrong: NAT does not encrypt traffic; protocols such as TLS and VPNs do that.
DNS translates domain names into IP addresses.
DHCP assigns IP addresses to devices on a network.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 21
note: Neil Core 1 mock exam (220-1101). NAT is not named in the current objectives; closest is 2.6 private and public addresses.

stem: Which type of IP address is assigned to devices that are connected to the internet?
explanation: Public addresses are assigned to devices that connect directly to the internet. They are globally unique and routable on the internet, so devices on different networks can communicate with each other.
whyWrong: Private addresses are used only inside internal networks and are not routed on the internet.
Loopback addresses, such as 127.0.0.1, refer to the local device itself.
Reserved addresses are set aside for special uses and are not assigned to internet hosts.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 41
note: Neil Core 1 mock exam (220-1101).

stem: Which range of IP addresses is reserved for use as private IP addresses within internal networks?
explanation: The range 10.0.0.0 to 10.255.255.255 is the Class A private address range. It can be used only inside internal networks, because routers on the internet drop packets with private addresses.
whyWrong: The 179.16.0.0 to 179.30.255.255 range is public address space, not a private range.
The 212.16.0.0 to 212.16.255.255 range is public address space, not a private range.
169.254.0.0 to 169.254.255.255 is the APIPA range that devices assign themselves when no DHCP server answers.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 49
note: Neil Core 1 mock exam (220-1101).

stem: What is the purpose of Automatic Private IP Addressing (APIPA) in a network?
options: To assign globally routable IP addresses to devices in a private network
To automatically assign public IP addresses to devices in a network
To provide temporary IP addresses when a DHCP server is unavailable
To enable communication between devices in different private networks
explanation: APIPA lets a device assign itself an address from 169.254.0.0 to 169.254.255.255 when it cannot reach a DHCP server. The address gives only limited connectivity on the local network, and it shows that the computer could not get an address from DHCP.
whyWrong: APIPA addresses are not globally routable, so they cannot be used on the internet.
APIPA does not assign public IP addresses.
APIPA works only within a single network segment, not between different private networks.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 50
note: Neil Core 1 mock exam (220-1101).

stem: Which of the following is a group of Windows desktop computers located in a small area?
explanation: A local area network (LAN) is a group of computers, such as a SOHO network, located in a small area. Larger network types join LANs over a city or a wide region.
whyWrong: A WAN is one or more LANs spread over a large geographic area.
A PAN is a small network used by smartphones and other small computing devices.
A MAN is a group of LANs in a city-sized area.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 10: Network Types, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: What kind of cable and connector are used with cable Internet service to connect to the customer’s “modem”?
explanation: Cable Internet connections use an RG-6 coaxial cable that runs from a NID to the customer's cable modem. The cable is connected with an F-connector.
whyWrong: Twisted pair and RJ-11 are used by DSL or dial-up, not cable Internet.
802.11ax is a wireless LAN standard, not a cable and connector.
Fiber-based services might use an ST connector, but cable Internet uses coaxial cable.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 10: Network Types, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: Which of the following might make use of Fibre Channel connections?
explanation: A storage area network (SAN) often uses Fibre Channel connections and switches to connect NAS points and other data storage devices into a very fast network. It carries storage traffic separately from the regular LAN.
whyWrong: A WAN connects two or more LANs over a large area.
DSL is a type of Internet service over telephone lines.
Cable Internet is a type of Internet service over coaxial cable.
A WISP is an Internet service provider that uses wireless technology.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 10: Network Types, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: Your client has three business locations within the city limits. All three locations need to be networked. The vendor’s network requirements for all three locations include a minimum data transfer rate of 1 Gbps. Which of the following network types should you MOST LIKELY use for the internal office communications and the office-to-office network communications? (Select the two best answers.)
explanation: You would most likely use a LAN (local area network) for internal office communications and a MAN (metropolitan area network) for office-to-office communications within the city. The MAN requires a data communications provider. Both can handle 1 Gbps.
whyWrong: A SAN connects NAS devices and RAID arrays at high speed, not offices.
A WAN connects LANs over large geographic distances, perhaps at speeds lower than 1 Gbps.
A PAN connects Bluetooth devices in an ad hoc manner.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 14

stem: Which of the following are advantages to using a SAN? (Choose two.)
options: More storage space on the network
explanation: Storage area networks (SANs) provide block-level data storage, which is more efficient, and they give servers faster data access while reducing load on the main network. They are also easy to expand.
whyWrong: A SAN does not by itself add more storage space, although it is easy to expand.
A SAN does not perform automated backups, although it can make backups easier to set up.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 6: Networking Fundamentals, Review Questions question 15

stem: You are setting up a small office network for a client. Which Internet service would you recommend to provide the BEST speed?
explanation: Of the options listed, fiber provides the best speed. DSL and cable provide similar speeds to each other but cannot match fiber.
whyWrong: DSL runs over telephone lines and is much slower than fiber.
Cable is faster than DSL in many areas but still cannot match fiber.
Satellite is the slowest of the options listed and has high latency.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 9: Wireless and SOHO Networking, Review Questions question 7

stem: Of the following four Internet connection options, which typically is most likely to have the highest latency?
explanation: Though newer low-orbit satellite access can be similar to other broadband methods, satellites in a geosynchronous orbit have much higher latency. The signal must travel more than 35,000 km up to the satellite and back down again.
whyWrong: Cable is a wired broadband connection with low latency.
Fiber optic usually has the lowest latency of these options.
DSL runs over the local phone line and has low latency.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 21: The Internet, Chapter Review question 1

stem: What advantage does WISP have over fiber optic?
options: WISP is faster than fiber optic.
WISP is cheaper to deploy, so it’s more likely to be available in smaller communities.
Fiber optic is more likely to be disrupted during rainstorms.
None. WISP has no advantages over fiber optic.
explanation: Because a WISP does not need to run cable to every home or business, it can be easier and cheaper to deploy in less populous areas. A wireless internet service provider sends the signal by radio from towers to an antenna at each customer site.
whyWrong: Fiber optic is faster than WISP service.
Fiber is not affected by rain; radio links such as WISP are the ones that weather can disrupt.
WISP's lower deployment cost is a real advantage in small communities.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 21: The Internet, Chapter Review question 3

stem: What advantage does satellite have over cable for connecting to the Internet?
options: Cable degrades in stormy weather; satellite does not.
Cable requires you to be within 18,000 feet of a central switch.
Cable is limited to areas with cable installed; satellite is not.
explanation: Satellite cuts you loose from the wires: it works anywhere with a clear view of the sky. Cable internet is available only where a cable company has run its lines.
whyWrong: Cable is usually faster than satellite internet.
Satellite, not cable, is the connection that rain and storms can disrupt.
The distance limit from a central office applies to DSL, not cable.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 21: The Internet, Chapter Review question 6

stem: Which of the following cellular data technologies is often considered 4G?
explanation: Long Term Evolution (LTE) is usually considered a 4G cellular data technology. It replaced the 3G technologies on most cellular networks before 5G arrived.
whyWrong: EDGE is an older 2G-era (2.5G) data technology.
UMTS is a 3G cellular technology.
CDMA is a channel access method used by 2G and 3G networks.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 21: The Internet, Chapter Review question 9

stem: On the 70th anniversary of Edmund Hillary’s climb to the summit of Mount Everest, a team from New Zealand plans to follow in his footsteps. Some of the locations that they will visit en route will have very poor connectivity for cell phones. Which of the following would you recommend that they use for communications?
explanation: Satellite communication devices connect to satellites above the earth, so they work in places where there are no cell phone masts. This makes satellite the right choice in remote mountain areas.
whyWrong: A carrier pigeon is not a real communication option for a modern expedition.
DSL needs a wired telephone line, which does not exist on a mountain.
A hotspot shares a cellular or Wi-Fi connection, so it fails where there is no cell coverage.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.4 question 11
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.4 (mobile connectivity); current 2.7 internet connection types (satellite).

stem: Which of the following technologies allows virtual servers to connect to high-speed storage?
explanation: A storage area network (SAN) is a dedicated high-speed network of storage devices. Servers, including virtualization hosts, use it to store their data and virtual machines.
