whyWrong: A PAN is a personal area network for devices close to one person, such as Bluetooth earbuds and a phone.
A cluster is a group of servers that work together for high availability; it is not a storage network.
RAID 0 stripes data across the disks in one system for speed and gives no fault tolerance.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.2 question 7
note: Old 220-1101 2.2; SAN is now under 220-1201 2.7 Network types.

stem: Which of the following can be used as a bridge to connect two wireless networks over a distance of 25 miles?
explanation: Long-range fixed wireless uses directional antennas to link two sites over many miles, so it can bridge two wireless networks. It can use licensed or unlicensed frequencies, and it is the technology that a WISP uses to reach customers.
whyWrong: GPS finds a location from satellite signals; it does not connect networks.
Unlicensed describes the frequency band that a link uses, not a type of bridge.
Licensed describes the frequency band that a link uses, not a type of bridge.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.3 question 4
note: Old 220-1101 2.3 (long-range fixed wireless); closest current topic is 220-1201 2.7 Internet connection types (WISP).

stem: What type of network would be a single site with all users in close proximity, secure, and connected by one or more switches?
explanation: A local area network (LAN) covers a single site with users close together and is connected by one or more switches. It is an internal network under the organization's control.
whyWrong: A WAN connects networks over a large geographic area.
A MAN covers a city or metropolitan area.
A campus area network connects several buildings, such as a university campus.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.6 question 5

stem: What type of network is the internet an example of?
explanation: The internet is a wide area network (WAN) because it covers a very large geographic area. A WAN connects many smaller networks.
whyWrong: A MAN covers a single city.
A PAN connects devices around one person, for example over Bluetooth.
A LAN is confined to one site, such as a building.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.7 question 1

stem: A mountaineering team is going to climb Mount Everest for charity. However, once they are 1,000 meters above the base camp, they find that they cannot use their cellular phones to communicate with the admin team back in the base camp. How can they climb the mountain and still communicate with the base camp?
explanation: Satellite connections work in remote places with no cellular or cable coverage, because the signal goes to a satellite in orbit. A satellite phone or terminal lets the team keep in contact.
whyWrong: A cable modem needs a cable connection, which does not exist on a mountain.
GPS only receives location signals; it cannot send messages.
Local wireless networks need an access point nearby, which there is not on a mountain.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.7 question 2

stem: What is the main type of connection used by an iPhone 11?
explanation: A smartphone such as the iPhone 11 connects mainly through the cellular network, which is why it is called a cellphone. It can also use Wi-Fi when it is in range.
whyWrong: DSL is a wired internet connection over telephone lines for homes and offices.
The phone can use Wi-Fi, but only near an access point; its main connection is cellular.
An iPhone 11 does not connect to communication satellites.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.7 question 4

stem: Which of the following statements are true about a wireless internet service provider (WISP)? (Choose two.)
options: They manufacture the most modern wireless access points
They install long-range fixed-access wireless technology
They provide a bridge between the customer and their service provider networks
They monitor the wireless bandwidth for corporate customers
explanation: A wireless internet service provider (WISP) gives internet access over long-range fixed wireless links. The link bridges the customer's site to the provider's network.
whyWrong: A WISP is a service provider, not a maker of wireless access points.
A WISP provides the connection; it does not monitor the wireless bandwidth of corporate customers.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.7 question 5

stem: Which of the following BEST describes a WAN?
options: An unsecure network over a very large geographical area
A secure fast network with all users in close proximity
A boundary network that protects the LAN
explanation: A wide area network (WAN), such as the internet, covers a very large geographic area and is not controlled by one organization, so it is treated as unsecure. Traffic over it should be protected, for example with a VPN.
whyWrong: A secure, fast network with users close together is a LAN.
A boundary network that protects the LAN is a screened subnet (DMZ).
Two of the statements describe other networks, so all of them cannot be true.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.7 question 6

stem: A small solicitor’s firm has just moved into a listed building. They are not allowed to drill into the walls and have paid a contractor to install a wireless router that connects all of the devices to the wireless network, meaning they do not need physical cables. What type of network has the contractor implemented?
explanation: A wireless local area network (WLAN) connects the devices at one site through a wireless router or access point, with no network cables in the walls. It is a LAN that uses Wi-Fi.
whyWrong: A LAN usually means cabled devices; the wireless version is a WLAN.
A PAN connects devices around one person, such as earbuds and a smartphone over Bluetooth.
A WAN covers a large geographic area, not one office.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.7 question 8

stem: A company’s telephone line has failed due to adverse weather, and their internet connection has been subsequently lost. What type of internet access must they be using for this to occur?
explanation: Digital subscriber line (DSL) carries internet traffic over the telephone line. If the telephone line fails, the DSL internet connection fails with it.
whyWrong: Satellite internet uses a dish and a satellite link, not a telephone line.
Fiber uses optical cables, not telephone lines.
A cable modem uses the coaxial cable TV network, not telephone lines.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.7 question 9

stem: Which type of network is typically confined to a small geographic area, such as an office building or campus?
explanation: A local area network (LAN) covers a limited area, usually within a building or a campus. It lets devices in that area share resources and communicate with each other.
whyWrong: A WAN covers a large geographic area and connects networks in different places, such as the internet.
A PAN connects personal devices in close range of one person, such as with Bluetooth.
A MAN covers a city or metropolitan area, connecting sites across the city.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 44
note: Neil Core 1 mock exam (220-1101).

stem: Which type of network spans a large geographical area and connects multiple LANs?
explanation: A wide area network (WAN) spans a large geographic area and connects multiple LANs. It lets offices in different cities or countries communicate and share data.
whyWrong: A LAN is confined to a small area such as a building or campus.
A PAN connects personal devices in close range of one person, such as with Bluetooth.
A MAN connects networks across a single city, which is smaller than a WAN.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 45
note: Neil Core 1 mock exam (220-1101).

stem: Which tool is used to test a network adapter without a network connection?
explanation: To test a network adapter without a network connection, you use a loopback plug. It simulates a network connection and can also be used to test a switch port.
whyWrong: A punchdown tool punches individual wires down to a patch panel.
A cable tester tests the entire length of a terminated cable.
A tone generator and probe traces a cable and checks only one pair of wires at a time.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 11: Networking Tools, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: Your boss is concerned about overlapping wireless networks from neighboring companies using 802.11ac. Which tool should you use to analyze the problem, and which frequency should you display for analysis?
explanation: To analyze the problem, use a Wi-Fi analyzer. Because your boss is concerned about networks using 802.11ac, you should display the results for 5 GHz networks, the band 802.11ac uses.
whyWrong: A cable certifier checks long wired connections, such as from a patch panel to an RJ-45 jack, not wireless networks.
A loopback plug simulates a network connection, and 802.11ac does not use 2.4 GHz.
A Wi-Fi analyzer is the right tool, but 802.11ac networks run on 5 GHz, not 2.4 GHz.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 11: Networking Tools, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: What would be required to attach RJ-45 plugs to the ends of a single patch cable?
explanation: RJ-45 plugs are attached to cable ends with a tool called a crimper. It presses the plug's pins onto the individual wires and locks the plug onto the cable jacket.
whyWrong: A tone and probe kit traces hard-to-find cables and wires.
A multimeter can test the continuity of a patch cable but cannot attach plugs.
A cable stripper removes part of the plastic jacket to expose the wires.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 11: Networking Tools, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: Your organization is terminating Category 6 cable to a 110 block. Which of the following tools should you use to perform the task?
explanation: Use a punchdown tool to terminate the individual wires of a Category 6 cable to a 110 punchblock. The tool presses each wire into its slot and trims the extra wire.
whyWrong: A crimper connects plugs to the ends of a cable.
A cable stripper removes a section of the cable's plastic jacket.
A tone generator puts a tone on one end of a cable so a probe can find the other end.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 11: Networking Tools, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: Say that you are responsible for the network security of your organization. You decide to perform packet sniffing on your switch by using Wireshark. Which of the following tools will help you to do this?
explanation: A network tap intercepts network traffic and makes a copy of it for analysis with programs such as Wireshark. Use a quality tap, because a poor one can reduce network bandwidth for everyone.
whyWrong: A tone and probe kit traces signals on cables.
A wireless analyzer shows the frequencies used by nearby wireless networks.
A loopback plug simulates and tests a network connection but cannot copy traffic.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 11: Networking Tools, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: Which of the following best describes the MOST LIKELY reason for connecting a tone generator to an RJ-45 cable drop?
options: To confirm continuity of the conductors
To locate the position of the cable on a patch panel
To test the transmission quality of the connection
To validate proper wiring of the network jack
explanation: A tone generator is often used to locate cables, especially when many are in a small area. The technician connects the tone generator to the RJ-45 drop and uses the probe (an inductive amplifier) to find the other end at the patch panel. Together the two tools are called a tone and probe kit, or toner probe.
whyWrong: Confirming continuity of the conductors takes a cable tester or certifier, not a tone generator.
Testing transmission quality takes a cable certifier, because a tone generator only puts a tone on the cable.
Validating the wiring of the jack takes a cable tester, which checks each wire's position.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 15

stem: You need to make a patch cable to connect a computer to an RJ-45 wall jack. Which of the following tools should be used to attach the RJ-45 plugs to the patch cable?
explanation: Use an RJ-45 crimper to attach RJ-45 plugs to the ends of a patch cable. The crimper presses the plug's contacts onto the wires and secures the plug to the cable.
whyWrong: A punchdown tool terminates individual wires to wall jacks and patch panels.
A loopback plug tests a network adapter when plugged into its RJ-45 port.
A cable tester tests patch cables and longer LAN cable runs.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 49

stem: You believe that a network card is beginning to fail. Which of the following tools should you use to see if the network card is capable of sending and receiving data from an RJ-45 port?
explanation: A loopback plug is used to test the ability of a network adapter to send and receive. The plug gets plugged into the NIC, and then a loopback test is performed using troubleshooting software.
whyWrong: A toner probe traces a cable from one end to the other; it does not test a NIC.
A multimeter measures voltage, resistance, and continuity, not a NIC's ability to send and receive.
A cable tester verifies that a cable's wires are intact and correctly wired, not the adapter itself.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 15

stem: Troubleshooting a network connectivity issue takes you into the wiring closet, where you realize that none of the cables are properly labeled. Several are disconnected. Which tool should you use to determine where the cables run to?
explanation: A toner probe is used to trace a cable from one location to another. The tone generator is attached to one end of the cable, and the probe picks up the tone at the other end to identify it.
whyWrong: A loopback plug tests a network adapter's ability to send and receive, not where a cable runs.
A punch-down tool connects the wires of a cable to a wiring block such as a 110 block.
A cable tester verifies that a cable works properly but does not locate its far end in a bundle.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 16

stem: A network cable for a crucial server has failed. There are no pre-made Ethernet cables available, but there is bulk cable and connectors. Which tool do you need to use to make a new cable?
explanation: A crimper is used to make network cables. It attaches an RJ-45 connector to the end of bulk twisted-pair cable; a cable tester can then verify the finished cable.
whyWrong: A punch-down tool connects cable wires to a wiring block such as a 110 block, not to an RJ-45 plug.
A cable tester verifies a cable after it is made but cannot attach connectors.
A loopback plug tests a network adapter's ability to send and receive, not build cables.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 18

stem: What small device enables you to test a NIC’s circuitry?
explanation: A loopback plug tests a NIC's Ethernet port and circuitry. It sends the NIC's outgoing signal straight back into its receive pins, so a diagnostic can confirm the port works.
whyWrong: Port tester is not a standard name for a device that tests a NIC's circuitry.
A multimeter measures voltage, resistance, and continuity, not a NIC's circuitry.
An integrated network and logic probe is not a standard network tool.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 19: Local Area Networking, Chapter Review question 4

stem: Which is a brand name of toner or tone generator?
explanation: Most techs call a toner or tone generator a Fox and Hound, the name of a popular brand of tone generator. The toner puts a signal on a wire, and the probe finds that wire at the other end of the run.
whyWrong: A TDR (time-domain reflectometer) measures cable length and finds breaks; it is not a toner brand.
UTP is a cable type, not a tone generator.
UDP is a connectionless transport protocol, not a tool.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 19: Local Area Networking, Chapter Review question 10

stem: Which of the following tools can be used to test a network card or switch port?
explanation: A loopback plug sends a port's transmit signal back to its receive pins, so it tests whether a network card or switch port can send and receive. A lit link LED shows that the port works.
whyWrong: A crimping tool attaches RJ45 plugs to cables; it does not test ports.
A cable stripper removes the cable jacket.
A punchdown tool terminates wires on the IDC blocks of a patch panel.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.8 question 1
note: Book explanation mentioned pliers, which are not an option; the crimping tool is described instead.

stem: Which of the following tools will be used by a network administrator to score the cable jacket and remove it from the cable so that it can be attached to an RJ45 plug?
explanation: A cable stripper scores the outer jacket of a cable so it can be pulled off and the wires exposed. The wires can then be put into an RJ45 plug and crimped.
whyWrong: A crimper presses the RJ45 plug onto the wires after the jacket is removed.
Pliers grip objects and would cut or crush the wires instead of scoring the jacket.
A loopback plug tests network ports.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.8 question 2

stem: What type of tool would be used to terminate wires into an IDC block?
explanation: A punchdown tool pushes each wire into an insulation displacement connector (IDC) block and trims the extra wire. It is used on patch panels and wall jacks.
whyWrong: A crimping tool attaches RJ45 plugs to the end of a cable.
A cable stripper removes the cable jacket.
A cable tester checks the wires of a finished cable.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.8 question 3

stem: The CEO of a company is unable to obtain a network connection. The ports on the patch panel are not labeled. Which network tool will the system administrator use to identify the port that the CEO is using?
explanation: A toner probe puts a tone on the cable at the CEO's wall jack, and the probe picks up the tone at the patch panel. This identifies which unlabeled port the cable connects to.
whyWrong: A crimping tool attaches RJ45 plugs to cables.
A punchdown tool terminates wires on IDC blocks.
An OTDR locates faults in fiber-optic cables.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.8 question 4

stem: Which of the following is the cheapest solution to monitor outbound traffic in an Ethernet network?
explanation: A network tap copies the traffic on an Ethernet link to a second port, so a monitoring device can analyze it. It is a simple, low-cost way to monitor traffic.
whyWrong: A loopback plug tests a network card or switch port.
A spectrum analyzer measures radio signals across a frequency range in wireless networks.
A toner probe traces a cable to its port on the patch panel.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.8 question 5

stem: A network engineer found that the RJ45 connection on an Ethernet cable had come loose and wanted to replace the RJ45 plug. Which of the following tools would they use to carry out this task?
explanation: A crimping tool presses a new RJ45 plug onto the wires of the cable, in the T568A or T568B order. The pins of the plug then make contact with the wires.
whyWrong: A punchdown tool terminates wires on IDC blocks, not in RJ45 plugs.
A cable stripper removes the jacket but does not attach the plug.
Pliers grip objects and cannot seat an RJ45 plug correctly.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.8 question 6

stem: A system administrator has a problem with their wireless access point. To troubleshoot the problem and measure the signal strength, what tool should they use?
explanation: A Wi-Fi analyzer, often software on a laptop or phone, shows the wireless networks nearby, their channels, and their signal strength. It helps find weak coverage and channel overlap.
whyWrong: A protocol analyzer captures and decodes packets; it does not map wireless signal strength.
A bandwidth monitor measures how much network bandwidth is in use.
Radio frequency interference is a problem that affects wireless signals, not a tool.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.8 question 7
note: Book explanation described RFID for the radio frequency interference option; whyWrong rewritten.

stem: What tool should a network administrator use to measure whether a cable in a wall socket has a permanent connection to a patch panel?
explanation: A cable tester is connected to both ends of a cable run and checks each wire for continuity and correct order. It confirms that the cable in the wall socket connects to the patch panel.
whyWrong: A loopback plug tests a network card or switch port, not a cable run.
A bandwidth monitor measures traffic levels, not the wiring of a cable.
An OTDR tests fiber-optic cables, not copper runs to a wall socket.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.8 question 8

stem: Which tool is commonly used to troubleshoot a fiber optic cable?
explanation: An optical time domain reflectometer (OTDR) is a tester for fiber optic cables. It sends light pulses into the cable and measures the reflections to find breaks or points of signal loss.
whyWrong: Wire cutters cut cable; they cannot test it.
An Ethernet cable tester checks the wire pairs of copper twisted pair cable, not fiber.
A multimeter measures voltage, current, and resistance in electrical circuits, not light in a fiber.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.1 question 2
note: The OTDR is not named in 220-1201 2.8; tagged with cable tester as the closest tool. Old objective 220-1101 3.1 (cables and connectors).

stem: Which of the following tools is commonly used to add lines to the demarcation point (demarc)?
explanation: A punchdown tool presses wires into the terminals of a punchdown block, such as the blocks at the demarc, and trims the extra wire. It makes a secure connection for each line added.
whyWrong: A wire stripper only removes insulation from wires.
A cable tester checks a cable for continuity and wiring faults but does not attach wires to a block.
A crimping tool attaches connectors such as RJ45 to cable ends, not wires to a punchdown block.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.1 question 5
note: Old objective 220-1101 3.1 (cables and connectors).

stem: What tool is commonly used to create an RJ45 cable?
explanation: A crimping tool attaches RJ45 connectors to the ends of Ethernet cables. It presses the connector pins into the wires to make a secure and reliable connection.
whyWrong: A wire stripper only removes the insulation; it cannot attach the connector.
A punchdown tool connects wires to a punchdown block or keystone jack, not to an RJ45 plug.
A multimeter measures voltage, current, and resistance; it does not build cables.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.1 question 9
note: Old objective 220-1101 3.1 (cables and connectors).

stem: A junior IT technician has inadvertently cut the end of an Ethernet cable with a sharp knife. What three tools do you need to repair it?
options: Wire cutters, a crimping tool, and an RJ45 connector
Screwdriver, electrical tape, and an RJ45 connector
Soldering iron, heat shrink tubing, and an RJ45 connector
Pliers, a multimeter, and an RJ45 connector
explanation: Use wire cutters to cut the damaged end off and strip the outer jacket, then insert the wires in the correct order into a new RJ45 connector. The crimping tool then presses the connector onto the cable.
whyWrong: A screwdriver and electrical tape cannot terminate an Ethernet cable with an RJ45 connector.
Soldering and heat shrink tubing are not used to attach an RJ45 connector, which must be crimped.
A multimeter measures electrical values; with pliers it cannot properly attach an RJ45 connector.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.1 question 16
note: Old objective 220-1101 3.1 (cables and connectors).

stem: What is the purpose of using a Wi-Fi analyzer to troubleshoot wireless connectivity issues?
explanation: A Wi-Fi analyzer shows the wireless networks, channels, and signal strengths in an area. This helps identify sources of signal interference, such as overlapping channels or nearby devices.
whyWrong: A Wi-Fi analyzer only measures the wireless network; it does not make it faster.
Changing the Wi-Fi password is a security task that is done in the router settings.
Expanding coverage needs more access points or extenders, not an analyzer.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.7 question 8
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.7 (network troubleshooting) = current 5.5. Tagged to current 2.8 Wi-Fi analyzer.

stem: Which statement about near-field communication (NFC) is correct?
options: It works only within a few centimeters and is a subset of RFID
It connects devices up to 100 meters apart on the 5 GHz band
It needs a paired PIN before every transfer, like Bluetooth
It is used to link a laptop to a cellular network
explanation: NFC is a short-range wireless technology that works when two devices are a few centimeters apart. It is a subset of RFID, and smartphones use it for contactless payments and quick pairing.
whyWrong: A 100-meter range on 5 GHz describes Wi-Fi, not NFC.
Bluetooth pairing can use a PIN, but NFC transfers start when the devices touch or nearly touch.
Cellular connections use the provider's network and a SIM, not NFC.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 5: Wireless Technologies

stem: Which device is a termination point for a building's network cables, with RJ-45 ports on the front and 110 IDC punchdown points on the back?
explanation: A patch panel terminates the building's twisted pair cables: each cable is punched down on the back, and short patch cables connect the front RJ-45 ports to the switches. It sits in a wiring closet or server room and makes patching ports easier and more reliable.
whyWrong: A switch forwards frames between ports; it does not terminate the building's cable runs.
An optical network terminal converts a provider's fiber signal at the customer site.
A cable modem connects to the provider's coaxial cable for internet access.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 8: Network Devices

stem: A customer's internet service comes in through an RG-6 coaxial cable from the provider. Which device connects the SOHO router to this service?
explanation: A cable modem has an RG-6 port for the provider's incoming coaxial cable. It connects to the computer or SOHO router through an RJ-45 port and a twisted pair patch cable.
whyWrong: A DSL modem uses the telephone line through an RJ-11 port, not coaxial cable.
An optical network terminal is used with fiber service, not coaxial cable.
A patch panel terminates internal cable runs; it does not connect to a provider.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 8: Network Devices

stem: Which port does a DSL modem use to connect to the provider's line?
explanation: A DSL modem uses the customer's telephone line, so it connects through an RJ-11 port. Its RJ-45 port then connects to the computer or SOHO router.
whyWrong: An RG-6 F-type connector is used by cable modems for coaxial service.
The RJ-45 port connects the modem to the local computer or router, not to the provider's line.
LC is a fiber connector, used with fiber service, not DSL.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 8: Network Devices
